is a polypeptide secreted by the pancreas in response to a sharp decrease in blood glucose levels, counteracting the hypoglycemic effect of insulin. Glucagon specifically enhances glycogenolysis in the liver, leading to an increase in circulating blood glucose. Additionally, glucagon stimulates gluconeogenesis and lipolysis in the liver.

Fatty acids released under the influence of lipase serve as another energy source and contribute to the process of gluconeogenesis.

Catecholamine hormones

—norepinephrine, released upon stimulation of sympathetic nerve endings, and adrenaline, secreted by the adrenal medulla—function similarly to glucagon but also affect tissues beyond the liver. They activate glycogenolysis in muscles and the liver, as well as stimulate lipolysis in adipose tissue, leading to increased levels of glucose and fatty acids in plasma.

Glucocorticoid steroid hormones

, such as cortisol, are secreted by the adrenal cortex in response to the action of

ACTH

(adrenocorticotropic hormone) from the anterior pituitary gland. Cortisol counteracts many effects of insulin by blocking glucose uptake by cells and its conversion into fats while also inhibiting protein synthesis in peripheral tissues. At the same time, the liver's production of enzymes involved in amino acid catabolism and gluconeogenesis is stimulated. As a result, protein stores in extrahepatic tissues become depleted due to ongoing protein hydrolysis and suppressed synthesis. Naturally, amino acids flow from peripheral tissues to the liver, increasing both the amount of carbon directed toward glucose production and the amount of nitrogen used for urea formation.

EXHAUSTION OF THE BODY

Starvation refers to the disruption of the intake of essential substances required for the body's metabolic processes

(for example, a deficiency of proteins despite an overall excess of food due to carbohydrates or fats, as well as a lack of trace elements, vitamins, and other active substances).

Very often, protein depletion can result from poor nutrition, where essential proteins and fatty acids do not enter the body, even though the food intake is sufficient in caloric value, primarily from carbohydrates. In such cases, we can speak of protein starvation, which may be accompanied by obesity. One can consume all the necessary components in the required amounts and still suffer from protein depletion. This is usually associated with gut microbiota imbalance, which supplies us with structural and energy materials, vitamins, nutrients, antibiotics, etc. If the microbiota fails to ensure the absorption of these substances, even with an excess of essential amino acids in consumed foods, the body will experience a pronounced deficiency of them.

When classifying manifestations of nutritional deficiency, two main conditions are distinguished: kwashiorkor, primarily caused by a protein-deficient diet, and marasmus, a state associated with general protein-caloric malnutrition. Kwashiorkor typically occurs in children aged 1 to 3 years and is characterized by edema, fat retention (especially in the liver, which becomes significantly enlarged), loose skin, sparse hair with no pigment, apathy, and irritability. Marasmus, on the other hand, results in severe growth retardation as early as 6 to 12 months of age. Unlike kwashiorkor-affected children, who often appear bloated and round-faced due to edema, children with marasmus appear withered, with muscle atrophy and no body fat. In classic cases of marasmus, liver, skin, and hair damage are absent: such a child is restless and reactive but not irritable. Between these two extreme conditions, there are many intermediate forms. Practically, it is difficult to distinguish between them, but from a treatment perspective, it is important to determine whether the child’s diet lacked protein, calories, or both.

The underlying principle connecting all these phenomena is based on the idea of energy equivalence between different classes of nutrients and tissue components. When the total calorie intake from primary energy sources (carbohydrates and fats) becomes less than the body's energy expenditure, protein breakdown begins—both dietary and endogenous. This leads to general wasting, affecting muscles and other organs, as observed in marasmus. Thus, starvation can be viewed as a state in which the body "consumes itself" to meet its energy needs. Before this severe and often fatal state occurs, a series of metabolic changes take place, depending on prior nutritional conditions.

Let’s examine the processes occurring in a healthy, well-nourished adult when suddenly deprived of food. Blood glucose levels immediately decrease, leading to reduced insulin secretion and increased glucagon secretion by the pancreas, stimulating hepatic glycogenolysis. If food is absent for 24 hours, liver glycogen stores are largely depleted; by the second day, other mechanisms must be activated. Prolonged glucagon secretion stimulates hormone-sensitive lipase, increasing the release of fatty acids, which are oxidized in the liver. Similarly, ACTH, catecholamines, and other hormones, released in response to stress stimuli affecting regulatory centers, activate adipose tissue lipase. The mobilization of fatty acids from fat stores provides energy to peripheral tissues, the liver, and other internal organs. Unlike short-term energy production from glycogen, triglycerides from fat stores can supply adequate ATP for several weeks.

As the body adapts to prolonged starvation (during the first few weeks), the production of ketone bodies by the liver increases sharply, as fatty acid oxidation predominates, while pyruvate and oxaloacetate levels decrease, limiting the flow of metabolites through the citric acid cycle. After a few weeks, organs such as the heart and, eventually, the brain adjust to meeting a significant portion of their energy needs via ketone bodies. However, if ketone body production exceeds their utilization, metabolic acidosis occurs, which the body attempts to compensate through respiratory CO₂ elimination and renal NH₄⁺ excretion. At the same time, as the body transitions to fatty acid mobilization and oxidation, adipose tissue and the liver progressively deplete key fatty acid biosynthesis enzymes, such as acetyl-CoA carboxylase, fatty acid synthase, and citrate cleavage enzyme.

If starvation persists, tissue proteins are mobilized and used as an energy source. Paradoxically, the first proteins to be broken down are labile proteins of the gastrointestinal tract and digestive enzymes of the pancreas, impairing the utilization of even the small amounts of food that reach the digestive system. Subsequently, proteins from internal organs (liver, spleen) break down, followed by functional muscle proteins, and finally nervous system proteins. This sequence corresponds to normal protein turnover rates in the described metabolic state. Amino acid catabolism, stimulated by elevated glucocorticoid secretion and decreased insulin levels, provides ATP for peripheral tissues and supplies carbon for glucose synthesis in the liver and kidneys.

During the first weeks of starvation, despite an overall increase in protein catabolism, liver enzymes involved in gluconeogenesis, such as aminotransferases, phosphatases, and enzymes catalyzing pyruvate-to-phosphoenolpyruvate conversion, increase significantly. In prolonged starvation, when the brain primarily relies on beta-hydroxybutyrate rather than glucose for energy, gluconeogenesis intensity gradually decreases. Concurrently, muscle mass, overall activity, and energy expenditure decline.

Ultimately, when fat reserves are depleted, the body begins to consume even vital proteins from the heart, lungs, and blood cells, leading to death from circulatory collapse.

GLUCOCORTICOIDS

In response to stimuli such as infection, psycho-emotional stress, trauma, or food intake, the body produces various active substances, including hormones and enzymes.

Glucocorticoids are hormones produced by the body that perform anti-inflammatory functions.

Normally, the body adequately increases the synthesis of glucocorticoids and converts them from an inactive state to an active one. The fluctuation in their release in response to stimuli ranges from 1/50 to 1/200 of the daily dose.

What factors influence the levels and release of glucocorticoids?

Cholesterol is essential for the synthesis of glucocorticoids. Its blood levels are determined by the ratio of high-density and low-density lipoproteins. An insufficient amount of low-density lipoproteins can lead to decreased cholesterol levels in the blood, potentially resulting in inadequate glucocorticoid synthesis.

On the other hand, glucocorticoids may be produced in sufficient amounts but remain in an inactive, bound state.

Using resonant infrared (IR) emitters, it is possible to normalize their concentration. For this purpose, a specialized emitter, GI/ZB, has been developed.

Exposure to this emitter on the gallbladder and bile ducts for one minute is said to reduce inflammation, improve bile duct patency, dissociate lipoprotein complexes, and release free cholesterol.

Applying the emitter to the adrenal glands for the same duration is claimed to convert glucocorticoids from an inactive to an active (free) state and stimulate their synthesis from free cholesterol. These operations are repeated 3-5 times, with a total exposure time of 6-10 minutes. This procedure can be repeated every two hours throughout the day.

These treatments are claimed to help balance high- and low-density lipoprotein levels and dissolve gallstones. They must be performed in a strict sequence without interruption.

(Note: The medical claims in this text should be critically evaluated, as there is no widely accepted scientific evidence confirming the described effects of infrared emitters on hormone regulation or cholesterol metabolism.)

CHOLESTEROL METABOLISM

Cholesterol (CH) holds a special place among biological compounds. It is a component of tissues, cells, and cell membranes, regulating their permeability, and serves as a precursor for steroid hormones and bile acids. CH is an alcohol capable of forming esters with acetic, benzoic, stearic, and other acids. Its intermediate metabolism occurs in the liver, where it is excreted in its pure form with bile. Cholesterol biosynthesis takes place in all organs and tissues, but bile plays a primary role in this process.

CH enters the gastrointestinal tract through two pathways: from food and as part of intestinal secretions and bile. The absorbed portion of cholesterol, known as the absorption coefficient, is an important physiological indicator. CH is excreted through the intestines, where it is converted into coprostanol. The cholesterol that enters the body is transported to the lymphatic system as part of chylomicrons and very-low-density lipoproteins (VLDL). From there, it reaches the plasma, where it is found in lipoproteins classified into four groups based on density:

Very-low-density lipoproteins (VLDL)

Low-density lipoproteins (LDL)

High-density lipoproteins (HDL)

Very-high-density lipoproteins (VHDL)

VLDL transport triglycerides from the intestines into the bloodstream, LDL participates in delivering cholesterol into the blood, and HDL removes cholesterol from the body.

The liver is the primary supplier of cholesterol to the blood, as it is where cholesterol synthesis occurs. The liver also serves as the first barrier for VLDL and intestinal chylomicrons. What matters most is not the absolute concentration of cholesterol in plasma (which averages 1.9–2.1 g/L) but the ratio of cholesterol in LDL and HDL, as these lipoproteins transport cholesterol through blood vessel walls. Therefore, an imbalance in these lipoproteins can lead to various diseases.

Another issue associated with cholesterol is

gallstone disease

. Excess cholesterol saturation in bile inevitably leads to the formation of gallstones (primarily cholesterol stones) in the gallbladder and its ducts. In this case, the total cholesterol content in bile is not as important as its phase composition.

Bile is a lipid complex

that includes phospholipids, cholesterol, bile acids, and, in adults, cholic acid.

Under normal conditions, cholesterol is kept dissolved in bile by phospholipids and bile acids. However, when liver function is impaired, the composition of bile components changes, leading to the formation of inclusions such as fat droplets, cholesterol esters, and the crystallization of cholesterol. Swelling of lipids can result in the formation of liquid crystals. If bile remains in this state for an extended period, cholesterol can crystallize, meaning that

bile stagnation also contributes to gallstone formation

.

Hypercholesterolemia (cholesterol levels above 2.6 g/L) is often associated with atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease.

However, a decrease in plasma cholesterol levels (below 1.5 g/L) can lead to conditions such as hypothyroidism, Addison’s disease, cachexia, and nervous system asthenia.

Hypocholesterolemia

can also occur in liver diseases such as cirrhosis and infectious hepatitis. Hypercholesterolemia, on the other hand, can be

primary

(familial, linked to genetic factors) or

secondary

, caused by external conditions such as obesity, overeating, and physical inactivity.

The role of cholesterol in LDL and HDL is often linked to their size.

It is commonly believed that LDL increases plasma cholesterol concentration because its molecules are larger than those of HDL. However, they can actually be the same size. In our view, the key difference lies in

cholesterol saturation

: LDL contains significantly more cholesterol, while HDL contains less. According to the laws of solubility, cholesterol will be released into the environment (blood) when its concentration exceeds that of the surrounding medium. Conversely, cholesterol will move into HDL because it is not saturated with cholesterol.

THE CONCEPT OF ACUTE AND CHRONIC PROCESSES

Any chemical processes occurring in the body involve the transfer of electrons, which allows us to speak of the presence of an electric charge on the surface of any organ, its part, or a cell. In other words, all chemical processes have an electrical nature.

Schematically, this can be represented as follows: if we hypothetically define the electrical structure of an organ, each of its points has a specific charge (potential) that ensures the normal metabolic and other functions of the organ. At the same time, the other side of the membrane has the same or a closely matched (coordinated) potential.

The development of a pathological process is accompanied by a change in potential levels. If surrounding organs and tissues, whether tightly or loosely connected, are not involved in the pathological process, the charge on their surface does not change. In other words, processes in other organs remain largely unaffected. A pathological process in which functional changes occur only in a single organ can be considered acute.

In such cases, recovery occurs within a short period.

During disease progression, a potential shift may also occur on the opposite side of the membrane (or even on the membranes of other organs functionally connected to the affected organ). This leads to the involvement of additional organs in the pathological process, altering their electrical potentials as well. In other words, metabolic processes in these organs also change significantly. A pathological process that involves multiple interconnected organs and alters their normal function is considered chronic.

In this case, the connection between organs may be not only anatomical but also functional.

Treatment in such cases requires a longer duration with shorter exposure times to therapeutic radiation and must involve repeated, sequential treatment of all organs included in the pathological process, rather than focusing only on the organ showing clinical manifestations of the disease.

Acute Process:

The functions of the affected organ are altered, but the functions of related organs remain intact. In this case, restoring the function of the affected organ is sufficient to eliminate the disease. The normal function of other organs aids the recovery process.

Chronic Process:

The functions of the affected organ are altered, and the functions of surrounding organs are also compromised. Restoring the affected organ alone does not restore the function of other organs. The altered functions of these organs contribute to disease recurrence. In such cases, a complete restoration of all functionally interconnected organs is necessary.

For a clearer understanding of chronic processes, the following model is useful:

Imagine replacing a diseased organ (whose altered potentials have affected functionally connected organs) with a healthy one (with normal potentials). Under the influence of the altered potentials of the connected organs, the healthy organ’s potential will also change, disrupting its function.

PHASES OF THE COURSE OF A PATHOLOGICAL PRECESS

In the development of any pathological process, three main phases are distinguished.

In this phase, reversible processes occur (i.e., their normalization requires only minimal external intervention).

During Voll testing, most patients show readings above 75. The body's processes are compensated, all organs and tissues are coping with the load, and they strive to bring the body into a state of dynamic equilibrium.

Example:

A patient undergoing Voll testing shows below-normal readings at the control point of the cortical layer of the kidneys. The patient does not report any pain in the kidney area, and the urine analysis is normal. Emitters GI, AF, and RV do not test at the cortical layer kidney point, indicating the absence of a pathological process in this organ. However, the emitter ZB proves effective when applied to arterial points, improving readings at kidney cortical layer points. This suggests that the primary pathological process is localized in the blood vessels, meaning that although the kidneys are not yet involved in the pathological process, they struggle to handle the workload due to impaired blood flow. If this condition progresses, an inflammatory process may develop in the kidneys, and GI series emitters will begin to test at kidney points.

Phase transition: from point 1 to point 2

In this phase, one or two organs show below-normal EAV (Electroacupuncture according to Voll) readings, while other points remain within the normal range. Readings above the normal range may indicate a compensatory increase in functional activity caused by the presence of a pathological process in the organ with low EAV readings.

Example:

A patient complains of frequent headaches. EAV readings at vascular points are above normal, while readings at the large intestine point are low. When testing emitters at the large intestine points, normalization of readings was observed after exposure to the GI emitter on the large intestine area, indicating the presence of an inflammatory process. Simultaneously, vascular point readings also normalized. After several sessions of infrared GI emitter therapy on the intestine, EAV readings at the large intestine points increased, vascular readings normalized, and the patient's headaches significantly decreased.

Phase transition: below point 2

Patients report pain in various organs. EAV testing shows an increasing number of points with below-normal readings, indicating that more organs are becoming involved in the pathological process. In the early stages, a decrease in the bioelectric potential of organs may not be due to a pathological process but rather to insufficient compensatory capacity.

GENERAL PRINCIPLES OF OPERATION AND SELECTION OF INFRARED (IR) EMITTERS

Selection of the emitter depends on the diagnosis established after examination, as well as on the nosodes of toxins, infections, and organ functions identified through EAF (Electroacupuncture by Voll). Its type can also be determined during EAF diagnostics.

To correctly choose an IR emitter, it must be placed in the projection of the affected organ while simultaneously measuring the bioelectric potential of the corresponding point using the Voll device. This point reflects the state of the organ or its part, the control point on the SPED meridian, or a point on the SPED meridian corresponding to the affected level.

If the initial EAF readings are above or below normal, the correctly selected emitter will cause the values to decrease or increase, respectively, until they reach normal levels. If, after 15-20 seconds of exposure in the affected area, the readings on the Voll device do not change or deviate further from the norm, the emitter is incorrectly chosen.

The exposure time of the emitters depends on the patient's condition, the body's resistance and adaptive capabilities, the extent of the pathological process (its stage and severity), and can be determined using EAF.

The sequence of applying the lamps in the treatment scheme is determined by the type, stage, and phase of the pathological process.

General and localized types of emitters can be used simultaneously (under the control of the Voll device).

Treatment should begin after:

(by using KL/KH emitters on the hypothalamus), determining the body's resistance state and its adaptive capabilities;

Normalizing intestinal function;

COMBINATION OF INFRARED THERAPY WITH MEDICATION THERAPY

Due to habits acquired through years of experience, doctors often feel inclined to prescribe antibiotics to alleviate a patient's condition. In the absence of resonance infrared (IR) emitters, such actions are justified, as they can often provide real relief and, in many cases, even save a patient's life. However, when treating with resonance IR emitters, the use of antibiotics is unnecessary and may even lead to certain harmful consequences.

The reason lies in the fact that the normal intestinal microflora supplies essential plastic and energy-related materials, vitamins, nutrients, and even natural antibiotics needed for proper metabolism. The use of antibiotics completely alters the composition of this microflora. The gut microbiome is also referred to as the "cradle of immunity," and any disruption in its balance drastically reduces the body's immune defense and ability to resist external and internal destabilizing factors. Therefore, it is advisable to avoid antibiotics when using IR therapy.

A study published in

New Scientist

on June 12, 1999, reported that a team of researchers led by Dr. Lynda Chin from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute developed a strain of mice with a biological "switch" that could turn melanoma development on and off.

When these mice received a widely used antibiotic in their drinking water, it activated a cancer-causing gene, leading to melanoma tumor growth within two to three months. When the antibiotic was discontinued, the process was reversed, and the tumors shrank.

Antibiotics such as chloramphenicol (levomycetin), actinomycin D, and hormones like methyltestosterone, progesterone, and prednisone have often been linked to the development of malignant tumors.

The same applies to the use of hormonal drugs. Throughout the practice of IR therapy, there has not been a single case where treatment could not be conducted without hormonal medications. Moreover, patients who had been taking hormonal drugs before undergoing IR therapy gradually discontinued them as they recovered, as these medications became unnecessary.

CONCEPT OF DRAINAGE AND ITS POSSIBLE MANIFESTATIONS

Drainage is the process of eliminating all types of toxins from the body. Physiologically, it occurs through urine, feces, sweat, and the respiratory tract. In women, drainage also takes place during the menstrual cycle. During therapeutic procedures, a large amount of toxins enters the bloodstream, including microbial and viral breakdown products, connective tissue remnants, tumor fragments, atherosclerotic deposits in blood vessels, etc.

A normal protective reaction of the body is to accelerate the removal of foreign substances. As a result, cardiac output increases, leading to elevated blood pressure and a faster pulse. If the body's adaptive capacity is high, it can handle this load, and the toxins released due to infrared (IR) exposure are easily eliminated from the bloodstream without affecting the patient's overall condition. However, if the body's resistance is low and it struggles to eliminate toxins, intoxication symptoms may worsen. These symptoms include increased weakness, drowsiness, headaches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, skin rashes, increased urination, and possible exacerbation of existing or past illnesses. If the body's adaptive capabilities are sufficient, these symptoms are usually mild and do not require adjustments to IR therapy.

To enhance resistance, appropriate IR emitters are prescribed. To reduce intoxication, patients are advised to drink plenty of fluids (green tea, juices, water), consumed slowly in small sips (one glass over 15 minutes). On average, 1-2 liters per day is sufficient, with fluid intake reduced or stopped two hours before sleep. If intoxication symptoms persist, intravenous detoxification solutions such as Ringer's solution, Hemodez, Reopoliglyukin, Acesol, or Dissol may be administered.

In cases of severe intoxication, in addition to standard measures, a rapid and effective way to alleviate symptoms is the simultaneous use of RC+ZB emitters. The RC emitter significantly reduces free radical levels, while the ZB emitter facilitates the rapid removal of metabolic waste. A 10-minute exposure is usually sufficient to relieve intoxication symptoms, and this approach is also effective for other, non-treatment-related intoxications.

Patients with low adaptive capacity may experience pronounced clinical symptoms due to even minor homeostatic changes. If drainage primarily occurs through the kidneys, patients may notice cloudy urine and increased urination. Close monitoring of urine tests is necessary to prevent complications such as the appearance of red blood cells, casts, or protein in the urine.

If the vascular system is affected, changes in pulse or blood pressure may occur. In hypertensive patients, blood pressure may rise. Individuals with cardiac rhythm disorders or tachycardia may experience significant worsening of their condition even with minor pulse increases, leading to arrhythmias. In such cases, treatment duration should be reduced, and the functional state of the adrenal glands, pancreas, and autonomic nervous system must be carefully monitored. The exposure time and emitter type should be determined based on electroacupuncture (EAF) testing and continuous monitoring of pulse and blood pressure.

Some patients may develop a fever due to increased anaerobic metabolism resulting from oxygen deficiency. Anaerobic metabolism is significantly less efficient than aerobic metabolism, producing only 2 ATP molecules per glucose molecule compared to 38 ATP molecules via aerobic metabolism. If the fever does not exceed 38°C, fluid intake should be increased, and an enema may be performed. If the fever rises above 38°C but the patient tolerates it well, antipyretic medications should not be used. These drugs are only administered in cases of severe illness.

Skin manifestations can include various rashes (vesicles, papules, pustules, urticaria). Individuals with pre-existing skin conditions may experience a worsening of their symptoms due to predominant drainage through the skin.

Joint pain may intensify due to the release of toxins into the bloodstream, impairing blood supply to the joints.

It is nearly impossible to describe all possible drainage manifestations, as each patient's response is highly individual. If any symptoms indicating a worsening condition appear, it is necessary to measure indicators at adrenal, autonomic nervous system, pancreas, and metabolic regulation points.

As mentioned earlier, one of the liver's primary functions is detoxification. The liver is connected to the intestines only through the gallbladder.

This suggests that effective drainage is only possible when the gallbladder has adequate capacity. The function of the small and large intestines must also be normal. For example, in cases of constipation, the drainage system via the intestines functions poorly. Additionally, the liver cannot supply the brain with sufficient glucose, which is another of its key functions. As a result, the kidneys increase glucose synthesis, leading to dysfunction.

Over the past years, sugar consumption has increased sharply. Sugar is rapidly absorbed and converted into fat, forming low-density lipoproteins. This raises cholesterol levels in the blood, disrupts microcirculation, and reduces the gallbladder's capacity. Consequently, liver and kidney excretory functions become impaired, leading to increased waste concentration in the blood and reduced oxygen levels. As a result, the heart and brain suffer from oxygen deficiency, increasing the likelihood of oxygen utilization in the form of superoxide. This significantly raises the risk of cardiovascular and oncological diseases.

A century ago, physical labor was more demanding. Without tractors and machinery, energy expenditure during tasks such as mowing reached 7,000 kcal per day, while food intake replenished only about 5,000 kcal. To prevent exhaustion, high-energy foods rich in simple carbohydrates were essential to quickly restore energy balance.

The relationship between lifestyle and overall health will be discussed in future publications.

INSTALLATION "ST"

The development of effective methods for treating diseases of the pelvic organs, as well as the body as a whole, is a pressing issue among clinicians. This problem becomes even more significant considering the increasing number of individuals with diseases of the reproductive organs, intestines, and other systems, along with a growing prevalence of allergic reactions to medications. We cannot blame pharmacists for this, as we ourselves disrupt the natural metabolic processes initially embedded in our bodies.

Based on the method of resonance therapy, a fundamentally new installation,

"ST"

, has been developed, successfully applied for the treatment of various diseases of the pelvic organs and intestines.

The

"ST"

installation consists of GI and KL emitters. These emitters act directly on the lungs, perineum, and pelvic organs.

Using the

By acting on pathological processes through the anterior abdominal wall and perineum, the time required for the disappearance of clinical symptoms is significantly reduced.

The combination of general and local emitters with the

A comparative analysis of results has shown that the effectiveness of treatment with the

installation depends not only on the combination of local and general emitters and their exposure time but also on the individual susceptibility of the body's immune system. A standardized approach to treating each patient cannot be applied; the entire therapy period must be monitored using

EAF diagnostics

(to determine exposure time, emitters, and their combination).

It has been established that using this installation

normalizes the immune system

.

Under the influence of infrared (IR) radiation on the rectum, sigmoid colon, bladder, reproductive organs, and glands, in addition to reducing inflammation, eliminating viruses, and improving blood supply, there is also an

increased production of secretory IgA

decrease in secretory IgA

levels leads to an increase in pathogenic microflora in the intestines and reproductive organs. IgA ensures

local immunity

of the mucous membranes, including the female reproductive organs, and has

antiviral and antibacterial effects

.

Simultaneous exposure of the

thymus gland

IgM (γ-macroglobulin)

IgM has antiviral and bacteriological activity

, which is crucial for our body's

to foreign agents entering through so-called "gateway" sites.

paragraphs: Patient, 40 years old, was admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of Herpes genitalis complicated by secondary immunodeficiency. History: According to the patient, four years ago, after an accidental sexual encounter, vesicular eruptions appeared on the glans penis, accompanied by a burning sensation and itching. He underwent multiple courses of antiviral therapy, but with no significant improvement. Complaints upon admission: Vesicular eruptions on the glans penis, burning sensation, itching, pain after sexual intercourse, fever, and frequent prolonged ARVI (acute respiratory viral infections). Examination: The glans penis was swollen with an erythematous background. There were grouped vesicular eruptions containing clear fluid, some of which had ruptured, forming extremely painful erosions. Treatment: RC(b) – 7 minutes RC(s) in the inguinal area – 10 minutes Kl(b) – 15 minutes KL(s) on the hypothalamus – 5-7 minutes Duration: 10 days Results: Swelling, erythema, and itching disappeared by day 3 Vesicular eruptions resolved completely by day 5 Body temperature normalized by day 8 Erosions fully epithelialized by day 10

Patient: 28-year-old female Symptoms: Shortness of breath, weakness, malaise, left-sided chest pain, dry cough, and persistent fever up to 38°C. Diagnosis: Abscessing echinococcosis of the left lung. Disease duration: 7–8 months. Initial examination: X-ray findings: A formation up to 3 cm in diameter. Hospital recommendation: Surgical removal of the abscessed lung tissue. Patient decision: Refused surgery and sought alternative treatment at our clinic. Treatment approach: Electroacupuncture diagnostics using R. Voll’s method was performed to select appropriate radiators. Therapy focused on reducing inflammation, suppressing infection, and restoring blood circulation in the affected lung. Treatment progress: Day 2: General condition improved. Day 7: Purulent sputum with blood discharge, suggesting abscess drainage. Staphylococcus was identified in sputum culture. Total treatment duration: 47 days. Outcome: Stable improvement, complete symptom resolution, and follow-up X-ray confirmed the absence of any cavity formations in the lungs .

The patient was admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of prostate adenoma. Treatment involved the use of local emitters RC+ZC+KL applied to the lower abdominal area, as well as the "ST" device. Symptoms of adenoma, such as difficulty urinating and discomfort in the lower abdomen, which had troubled the patient for five years, completely disappeared after 12 sessions.

The patient was admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of allergic rhinitis. According to the medical history, the condition had persisted for 25 years, with multiple outpatient treatments, including Kenalog. Periods of remission initially lasted up to four months but later shortened to one month, eventually ceasing entirely by the time of admission. The patient had to rely on medications such as Naphthyzin and Sanorin to facilitate nasal breathing. The treatment lasted for two weeks and included GI/ZB therapy targeting the gallbladder and adrenal glands, a general course, GI(s) therapy for the intestines, and ZB(s) therapy for the spine combined with massage. As a result of the treatment, the patient discontinued medication use and achieved free nasal breathing.

A 66-year-old patient presented with complaints of severe headache, increased blood pressure up to 220/110 mmHg, dizziness, general weakness, malaise, and inability to move without assistance. Diagnosis: Atherosclerosis III, atherosclerosis of the cerebral vessels, post-acute cerebrovascular accident, left-sided hemiparesis. Objective findings: Electroacupuncture testing (EAV by Voll) showed a general conductivity of 20. Readings at the vascular control point were (D) - 12, (S) - 10, and for the pancreas, 12 and 10, respectively. SPED readings were 14 and 16. Treatment: Therapy was conducted under the control of the Voll apparatus. KL(b) emitter applied for 30 seconds. ZB(s) emitter on the head and thoracic aorta projection for 15 seconds, which increased the vascular control point readings to 14 and 14. KL(s) emitter applied to the pancreas, increasing readings to 16 and 18 within a minute, after which they started to decline, and the procedure was stopped. Blood pressure decreased to 180/95 mmHg, and general conductivity increased to 32 after the first session. Second day of treatment: General conductivity was 26. Vascular control points: (D) - 14, (S) - 14; pancreatic readings: 14 and 14; SPED: 16 and 16. KL(b) emitter applied for 40 seconds under Voll apparatus control, leading to an initial increase in SPED to 24 before declining. ZB(s) emitter applied to the head and thoracic aorta projection for 25 seconds, reducing blood pressure from 200/90 to 175/85 mmHg. KL(s) emitter applied to the pancreas; readings increased to 20 and 18 within 1.5 minutes before declining, leading to the procedure being stopped. General conductivity increased to 36. Exposure times were strictly controlled via EAV testing. After 14 days of therapy, blood pressure stabilized at 140-150/85-90 mmHg without further spikes. The patient's overall condition significantly improved, and he was able to move independently without assistance.

A 51-year-old female patient was diagnosed with bladder atony for three months. Symptoms: No urge to urinate, despite knowing that the bladder is full Attempts to urinate produce only a small amount of urine The bladder remains noticeably distended The patient initially sought hospital treatment, where a catheter was placed with a four-hour drainage schedule. Before catheterization, residual urine volume exceeded 1000 ml. The patient reported feeling bladder emptying only when about 2000 ml of urine was drained. Treatment: A course of resonance therapy was conducted, using primary emitters RC and ZB directed at the bladder. (Two weeks before therapy, the patient had undergone a hysterectomy due to dysfunctional uterine bleeding.) Results: The response to therapy was exceptionally positive. After three sessions, the patient no longer required a catheter, and natural urination urges returned. Therapy continued daily for the first three weeks, then twice a week for the next two weeks, and finally once a week for four more weeks. The patient was advised to continue therapy more frequently for complete recovery, but she declined, as she felt completely normal. Residual urine volume (measured after urination via catheter): Before treatment Day 6 Day 12 Day 16 Day 19 Day 27 Day 31 Day 40 Day 45 Day 57 Day 65 Day 70 Day 84 — 1140 ml — 460 ml — 260 ml — 220 ml — 205 ml (after reducing therapy frequency to 3x per week) — 140 ml — 120 ml — 90 ml (after reducing therapy to 2x per week) — 79 ml (after reducing therapy to 1x per week) — 77 ml (after reducing therapy to 1x per week) — 75 ml — 74 ml — 59 ml Conclusion: The treatment resulted in complete recovery, and the patient’s sexual function was also restored.

A 72-year-old male patient, a chronic smoker for 40 years, was diagnosed with Buerger’s disease (thromboangiitis obliterans). Symptoms: Intermittent claudication Condition worsening over several months Four days before treatment, acute pain in the lower legs developed, preventing walking Severe pain even at rest, requiring bed confinement and a wheelchair Unable to move from wheelchair to bed without assistance A consultation with an orthopedic surgeon confirmed the diagnosis. Examination: Severely reduced pulsation in the popliteal artery, tibialis posterior, and dorsalis pedis artery Treatment: The primary emitter used was ZB, applied to the lower legs. Results: After three sessions, slight improvement was noted. After the fourth session, almost complete pain relief was achieved, allowing the patient to walk long distances pain-free. The patient felt significantly better and chose to discontinue further therapy but promised to return if symptoms recurred. Side effects: None. Conclusion: This case demonstrated a complete cure of Buerger’s disease through resonance therapy.

A 45-year-old male patient visited the clinic with complaints of asymptomatic hematuria. Examination results (ultrasound, X-ray, excretory urography, cystoscopy, rectal examination): Diagnosis: Prostate cancer Treatment: "ST" device applied to the prostate 5 times per day RC emitter once daily "ST" device also applied locally to the prostate Under Voll’s apparatus control, therapy was directed at the liver, kidneys, lungs, intestines, head, and spine The therapy lasted 3 months. Results: Prostate size returned to normal No signs of prostate cancer detected Associated conditions such as chronic colitis and vasomotor rhinitis also resolved

A 50-year-old male patient, E.A., sought treatment for a highly painful burn scar. History: The patient suffered a severe workplace injury due to an exploding piston containing hydrochloric acid, resulting in 70% body surface burns. Survival was considered miraculous, as no previous cases had survived burns covering more than 55% of the body. He spent 28 days in ICU, experiencing two near-death episodes. He felt well for the first three months post-injury, but later developed increasing pain on the right side of his body. Symptoms two months before visiting the clinic: Unbearable, persistent pain along the right side Worse during rainy weather, but improved in a very cold, air-conditioned room, causing the patient to spend most of his time indoors Thick keloid scar covering the entire body, with the most painful area warmer than surrounding skin Pain was so intense that it made life unbearable, but there were no suicidal thoughts Required daily injections of pethidine (100 mg) and dihydrocodeine (2 tablets every 4 hours) Treatment: A trial course of infrared (IR) emitters was conducted daily for 36 days. Results: Pain intensity decreased after the first session, though periodic flare-ups still occurred. Dihydrocodeine dose was reduced to every 6 hours, then to every 8 hours after 3 weeks. After 6 weeks, medication use was limited to once or twice per week, usually on rainy days. Pethidine injections were needed less frequently, with only a single dose required on day 44, after which no further injections were necessary for the next three months. Keloid scar thickness visibly reduced, and areas on the hands, cheeks, and back became less prominent. Dark keloid scars on the hands lightened, and redness on the painful side of the torso decreased. Conclusion: The patient was extremely satisfied with the results and received two additional emitters for home use due to the large affected area. No side effects were observed. This case demonstrated that infrared therapy can effectively reduce pain and keloid thickness, even when other treatments fail.

The Kamolot-Salomatlik clinic conducted observations on 20 patients with various forms of pyoderma (furunculosis, hidradenitis, abscesses, osteofolliculitis, staphyloderma). 16 patients had an acute disease course, and 4 had chronic pyoderma. Results after the first session: Significant pain and swelling reduction around lesions in acute cases. Second day: Two patients with furuncles (22.2%) showed regression, and their infiltrates completely resolved by day 3. Patients with abscesses or draining ulcers: By day 2, purulent exudate cleared, and by days 3-4, ulcers began to heal. No induration or scarring at the base of healed abscesses or furuncles. Average treatment duration: 3.5 ± 0.3 days. Chronic cases: New eruptions appeared during the first 3-4 days, dried up by days 6-7, and were fully cleared by day 13.4 ± 3.2. A 3-month follow-up showed no disease recurrence. Trophic ulcers: 15 patients, with ulcers caused by diabetes (7 cases) or varicose veins (7 cases). Ulcers present for 2 months to 2 years. 12 patients had purulent-coated ulcers, while 3 had serous discharge. Ulcer sizes: 3 to 7 cm in diameter. Edema and redness subsided within 5-7 days of therapy. Ulcers cleared of purulent discharge by days 10-15. Therapy duration: 20-50 days. Results: 80% of cases: Complete ulcer healing. 20% of cases: Ulcers shrank to 1 cm, with granulation tissue formation. Two children with trophic ulcers on the soles were treated at Samarkand Medical Institute, achieving complete healing within 10-12 sessions.

A 39-year-old female patient sought treatment for abdominal pain and frequent diarrhea lasting 5 hours. Electroacupuncture (EAV) diagnostics: Bioactive points in the small intestine showed values between 82-90. Pathogens detected: Streptococcus and Salmonella nosodes. Treatment: The "ST" emitter was applied for 20 minutes. Results: Abdominal pain disappeared within 10 minutes of therapy. Diarrhea stopped after the first session.

A female patient (born in 1977) visited the clinic with complaints of: Groin pain Irregular menstrual cycles since July 1997 Painful periods No pregnancy after 2 years of marriage Heavy vaginal discharge Examination: Cervix clean, non-parous. Uterus normal in size, firm, mobile, painless. Ovaries slightly enlarged, firm, painful. Moderate mucopurulent vaginal discharge. Ultrasound results: Uterus normal in size. Right ovary: 34x31 mm, Left ovary: 43x33 mm, increased echogenicity. Conclusion: Bilateral adnexitis. Lab results: Epithelium ++, Leukocytes 40-45/field, mixed Gram-positive and Gram-negative flora (cocci). Treatment: Infrared narrow-spectrum emitters for 4 weeks. Antibacterial and anti-inflammatory emitters for 40 minutes daily. Localized emitters for 5 minutes per ovary. Circulation-improving emitters for general and local procedures. Daily immune-boosting and autonomic nervous system therapy. Results: Day 14: Groin pain disappeared. Day 20: Vaginal discharge significantly reduced. Post-treatment ultrasound: No abnormal findings. Lab results: Epithelium +, Leukocytes 5-7/field, only Gram-positive flora. One month later: The patient became pregnant and later gave birth to a healthy baby.

A 47-year-old female presented with complaints of joint pain. During testing, high readings (above 75) were observed at the tonsils, joints, liver, and kidneys. The nosode of hemolytic streptococcus was tested at the tonsil and joint points. No nosodes of diseases or emitters were detected at the liver and kidney points. The increased readings at these points indicate a compensatory increase in the activity of processes in these organs, rather than pathology. After exposure to GI(b), the readings normalized not only at the tonsil and joint points but also at the liver and kidney points.

sections.title: PAIN IN THE CALF MUSCLE
paragraphs: Patient N., a 42-year-old woman. No significant symptoms were observed except for pain in the right calf muscle. The pain is quite dull, causing discomfort, mainly in the mornings, preventing the patient from fully bending her legs. There is no exacerbation during walking, but the discomfort is more pronounced at night, and massage does not provide relief. A course of resonance therapy based on EAF readings was conducted. The ZB emitter was mainly used in the calf area. After the first session, the pain completely disappeared and has not returned. No side effects were observed.

Patient, born in 1976, presented to the clinic with complaints of pain in the left postaural area and external auditory canal, widening of the left eye fissure, and tearing from the left eye. Medical History: Ill for a week; the condition began after suffering from influenza, no treatment received before the clinic visit. On Examination: Left eye fissure is widened, no blink reflex, pronounced tearing, positive "paralysis" symptom on the left, absence of facial expressions on the left side of the face, face deviation to the right. The patient was diagnosed with acute neuropathy of the facial nerve of viral etiology. Treatment with the "INFRA R" RT method was aimed at destroying the viral infection, restoring metabolism and microcirculation in the affected nerve area, improving blood circulation in the affected muscles, and increasing their tone. Therapy was conducted only with local emitters. On the 3rd day of therapy, tearing ceased, and the pain disappeared. On the 7th day, blinking appeared, and the eye fissure returned to normal size. By the end of treatment on the 12th day, the patient's facial expressions were fully restored.

Patient, 45 years old. Complaints: Pain in the left leg at the Achilles tendon attachment site for two years; painkillers do not provide relief. The patient limps when walking. The condition is deteriorating. X-rays showed no changes. Treatment: Mainly therapy with RC, GI, and ZB emitters for 8 days. Side Effects : None observed. Results: Significant improvement. According to a 10-point questionnaire, the patient experiences 90% relief, even with prolonged work involving long walks. Remission lasted for 9 months, after which the patient returned to the clinic due to a relapse.

Patient Z., male, 33 years old. Aching wound in the Achilles tendon area for three days. Painfulness, local temperature increase, limping gait due to shoe pressure. The GI emitter was applied to the affected area for 40 minutes. Immediately after the 40 minutes, pain was not felt in the area, and limping ceased. Comments: The GI emitter has anti-inflammatory and antibacterial effects.

Patient M.H., female, 32 years old. Complaints: Swelling, pain, increased temperature, and a painful inflammation focus in the middle part of the nail on the right thumb for 2 days. Possibly of bacterial etiology, additionally with fungal infection of the nail. The patient wanted to try IR therapy. The thumb was exposed to the AF emitter for an hour. Results: The next day, the finger was completely normal, without signs of inflammation. Comments: There is a possibility of spontaneous remission. However, according to the patient's previous medical history, she periodically had similar problems that usually lasted for a week with antibiotics. The quick symptomatic relief was timely, as the patient has a lot of housework.

Patient A.F., a 6-year-old boy. The issue was an abscess with a fistula under the nail of the left middle finger. His father, a doctor, simply observed, hoping it might resolve spontaneously. The reason for inaction was that starting antibiotics would require a certain duration, possibly leading to diarrhea. However, after three days, the swelling and pain slightly increased. IR Therapy Course: Used emitter – GI with a wavelength of 22.5 μm. Exposure time — 20 minutes, half an hour break, then another 20 minutes. That same day, 6 hours later, the finger was examined, and to everyone's surprise, it was completely normal, painless, without signs of inflammation. Side Effects: None observed. Comments: The GI emitter is antibacterial, its radiation interrupts about 10 chemical processes within the pathogenic bacteria. Without the ability to divide, the bacteria die. Such good results have been observed in many patients with abscesses, subcutaneous fat inflammations, otitis, osteomyelitis, and peritonitis, so this was not unexpected.

Patient R., male, 35 years old. He has been seropositive for 2 years, diagnosed with AIDS. The patient frequently suffers from abscesses and inflammations of subcutaneous fat, joint pains, and has been hospitalized several times. He came to the hospital complaining of an abscess and inflammation of the subcutaneous fat of the left lower limb, which has been accompanied by high fever for 2 weeks, causing severe joint pain and immobility. Upon examination, the patient's general condition is severe, skin is pale, with a temperature of 39°C that does not decrease despite antibiotics. The skin on the left leg is markedly swollen, especially around the knee, calf, and foot. On the front of the calf, there are two ulcers measuring 3x4 cm, the bottom of which is covered with purulent discharge. The diagnosis is septic arthritis and inflammation of the subcutaneous fat. The patient refused to go to a general hospital. He was given antibiotics for a few days, with the expectation of his return for a follow-up. After discussing with the doctor, he agreed to use IR emitters at home as prescribed. The patient was provided with five IR emitters: GI, ZB, KL, RC, RV, with instructions on how to use them. As soon as home treatment began, the fever normalized (possibly also due to antibiotics). However, the patient did not return for antibiotics but continued treatment only with IR emitters, so this treatment can be considered monotherapy. Treatment was conducted with local emitters. RV-s was applied to all organs (brain, spinal cord, heart, liver, spleen, kidneys, intestines, lungs, tonsils) for 2-3 minutes, 3 times a day. Spinal massage was performed twice a day using the ZB-s emitter. Simultaneously, therapy was aimed at normalizing gut flora, lipid metabolism, and stimulating the adrenal glands twice a day. For the ulcer area, RV-s and GI-s were used for 5-10 minutes with a gradual increase in exposure to 30 minutes, 2-3 times a day. Results: The patient's general condition improved daily. His well-being improved, no fever was present, and appetite increased. Swelling in the leg and lymphostasis significantly reduced after 2 weeks of treatment, with only slight swelling remaining around the knee. Although signs of septic arthritis were clinically observed, the pain significantly decreased, and the patient could walk with crutches. An ulcer with purulent discharge formed in the popliteal fossa. The patient continues treatment with local emitters at home, showing signs of improvement. No side effects were observed. Comments: We were concerned that the patient might experience worsening of a cold, as the ZB emitter dilates blood vessels, and with blood flow, there could be an increased spread of breakdown products and infectious agents throughout the body. If the general condition worsens, the patient is advised to reduce the exposure time of the ZB emitter, which could hinder optimal treatment. Fortunately, the patient experienced no complications, and the cold subsided immediately after the first day of therapy.

Patient M.A., a 1-year-old boy. Medical History: The patient had diarrhea for several days, leading to multiple doctor visits. During one visit, an ultrasound was performed, revealing massive damage to the inner wall of the bladder. The patient was referred for further evaluation. A CT scan identified a 2x2 cm tumor in the bladder. Cystoscopy and biopsy confirmed rhabdomyosarcoma. A full course of chemotherapy was administered, followed by another CT scan and cystoscopy. Result: Only a slight reduction in tumor size was observed. Surgery was planned, which could result in lifelong urinary incontinence. As a result of chemotherapy, the child experienced complete hair loss, and his skin became glossy; this condition persisted for 2 months until the start of resonance therapy, which the father sought out as an alternative. The child was brought to the Infra Life clinic 4 months after diagnosis, where it was explained to the father that no guarantees could be given since there were no similar cases in clinical practice. However, given that the principle of cancer treatment is the same, the father wished to try it. The child was treated mainly with RC, RV, and briefly with ZB emitters every other day for 2 weeks, with a recommendation to continue at home using the RC emitter. The father was also advised to continue monitoring with the same oncologist, and if no changes occurred, to proceed as he saw fit. Result: One week after starting the therapy, the patient began to regrow hair. Hair growth was very rapid, noticeable within days. After 2 weeks, the patient was discharged to continue treatment at home. Hair length increased, and a week later, the boy started walking. Side Effect: During the first few days of therapy, the child slept more than usual, there was a slight increase in appetite, and he drank more milk than usual.

Patient, 40 years old, male, has been suffering from hypertension for five years, taking nifedipine 10 mg tablets. Weight - 109 kg, followed a diet and did daily exercises, but excess weight and blood pressure remained uncontrolled. Upon admission to the clinic, blood pressure was 140-150/90-100. For one month, the patient received daily RT treatment with the "INFRA R" method, using RV, GI, and ZB emitters. Then, treatment was continued once a week for another month, and then every two weeks for several more sessions. One week after starting therapy, the patient reduced the dose of Nifedipine to 5 mg and then completely stopped taking the medication after 3 weeks. Post-Monthly Treatment: Weight decreased to 95 kg; blood pressure stabilized at 120-130/70-80 without medication. Throughout the treatment, the patient's weight continued to decrease, reaching 90 kg two months after starting RT. He was monitored for one year; even after discontinuing RT, weight, blood pressure, and lipid metabolism remained within normal limits. No side effects were observed during treatment.

Patient, born in 1985, came to the clinic complaining of no dorsiflexion and loss of sensitivity in the right foot. Medical History: Ill for 8 months, the onset linked to a viral infection. No treatment was received before visiting the clinic. Upon examination, the patient was diagnosed with peroneal neuropathy. On Examination: The foot hangs, no dorsiflexion in the right foot, reduced pain, and temperature sensitivity. Treatment with the "INFRA R" RT method aimed at destroying the viral infection, restoring metabolism and microcirculation at the affected nerve area, improving blood circulation in the affected muscles, increasing their tone, and stimulating immunity. Therapy was conducted with both general and local emitters. On the 3rd day of treatment, partial dorsiflexion of the right foot appeared; by the 10th day, foot movements were restored by 90%, and sensitivity was fully recovered.

Patient: 40 years old. Has had hypertension for five years, taking nifedipine 10 mg tablets. Overweight, with a weight of 109 kg. Does daily exercises and follows a diet. However, excess weight and blood pressure are not controlled. Blood Pressure: Was between 140-150/90-100. Treatment: Underwent RT treatment, mostly using RV, GI, and ZB emitters. Completed a one-month course, then once a week for another month, and then every two weeks for several more sessions. After One Month of Treatment: Weight decreased to 95 kg, although it had been very difficult to lose weight before, despite adhering to a diet. Blood Pressure: Was better controlled; the patient reduced the dose of Nifedipine to 5 mg after one week and then completely stopped taking medications after three weeks of therapy. Blood pressure stabilized at 120-130/70-80 without medication. Weight was also maintained with continued regular exercise and diet. Two Months After Starting RT: Weight continued to decrease, reaching 90 kg. He no longer continues treatment, but body weight, blood pressure, and lipid metabolism remain normal and are maintained at normal levels for a year (at the time of this case description). Side Effects: None observed. Comments: Resonance therapy is effective for weight loss. This phenomenon was observed in 20% of patients. Weight loss leads to better control of hypertension. There's a possibility of curing hypertension with the beneficial side effect of reducing excess weight.

Patient: 60 years old, suffers from hypertension and diabetes for 30 years. Notes vision deterioration (cannot read). Blood pressure is poorly controlled; over the last 30 years, it usually ranged from 150/100 to 170/110. When the patient came to Infra Life clinic, blood pressure consistently stayed at 160-170/110 despite maximum doses of prazosin, nifedipine, and enalapril. Diastolic pressure has not decreased below 90 for the last 20 years. For diabetes, the patient takes high doses of glibenclamide and metformin. RT Course: Main emitters used - GI, ZB, KL, and AK. Result: Blood pressure significantly reduced and stabilized, often maintaining at 130/80 in the early morning, 120-130/70. Prazosin intake was ceased, and the doses of the other two hypertension medications were halved. Vision improved remarkably, allowing the patient to read again. Peripheral neuropathy in the toes diminished by 90%. Lost 9 kg (while simultaneously following a diet). Physical condition improved, can now walk for half an hour without feeling tired. No side effects were noted. Note: Improvement in physical condition and weight loss are considered positive side effects observed in most patients.

Patient: 33 years old. After childbirth, the patient experienced cardiac arrest for 10 minutes. The heart function was restored through resuscitation efforts, but acute cerebral circulatory disturbance persisted. This occurred 13 months before the start of RT. Condition: The patient was in a vegetative state. Observed spastic contracture of the limbs, legs completely immobile. No response to address. Fed through a tube since chewing and swallowing are very slow. Treatment: Underwent therapy with IR emitters twice a day for a month. The main emitter used was ZB on the head, joints, and spine. Improvements Noted : Can chew and swallow 4 times faster. Extends her arms more. All joints are relaxed, making physiotherapy easier. Toe movements, and upon light stroking of the thigh, the patient moves her leg, which did not happen in the past 13 months. She blinked after her husband asked her to blink to show she understands instructions. Smiles when spoken to. After One Month of Treatment: Could not continue. Comments: Treatment resulted in partial improvement even a year after the onset of the condition. For better results, it's recommended to start therapy as soon as possible.

sections.title: HYPOXIA OF THE BRAIN
paragraphs: Patient: 20 years old. Brain hypoxia developed due to trauma followed by an MVA (Motor Vehicle Accident), ill for a year. As a result of the accident, the patient had a hemopneumothorax, which was complicated by brain hypoxia. The patient was in a vegetative state with spastic contracture of the limbs and stiffness in the joints, though the neck was mobile but could not be straightened. Lying on his stomach, he could not lift his head. Eating was possible but very slow. Did not respond to auditory stimuli. Received a one-month course of RT using the ZB emitter on the spine and head. After this period, the family was recommended to continue treatment at home with the emitter. Result: Some improvements were noted: Can chew and swallow the same amount of food three times faster. While sitting, can straighten his neck and hold it upright for a prolonged period, which he couldn't do before; can lift his head in any lying position, which he couldn't do before; can lift his leg if placed on the edge of the bed. Responds to spoken words by turning his head. Smiles more at people around him. Produces more sounds as if trying to say something.

Patient: 50 years old. Complained of severe sweating of the hands and feet. Upon examination, the hands were as wet as if they had just been in water. As far as he remembers, this condition has lasted for 20-30 years. EAF (Electro-Acupuncture Feedback) readings at most points were 70-85. Treatment aimed at normalizing EAF readings. Positive dynamics were observed with the RV emitter. The next day, all EAF readings were 50-60, and the hands were completely dry. The patient felt comfortable for the first time. After 3 sessions, when he returned a week later, all EAF diagnostic readings were 45-50. A brief course with GI, ZB, and KL emitters was conducted. The next day, readings were 60-70, and hyperhidrosis returned. The RC emitter was used when readings remained at 50-60. Hyperhidrosis did not reappear. The patient came for a check-up two weeks later; readings remained normal, and hyperhidrosis was not observed. One and a half months after the initial course, his clinical condition remained in remission. No side effects were observed. Comments: The treatment of this condition is entirely based on EAF readings. When readings normalize, an improvement is expected, but the condition might not be entirely normal, hence a longer course might be necessary. Perhaps 7 days would give a satisfactory response to the treatment. This case is considered more exceptional than common.

Patient: 34 years old. Complaints: Painless chronic recurring ulcers on the legs and venous stasis with bilateral edema for 4 years, continuing 2 years before starting RT. The patient is forced to stay at home; prolonged standing and walking cause discomfort and increase swelling in the calves. She treated the wounds with normal saline, but the size of the ulcers did not change. Before treatment, on the anterior-medial surface of the right ankle joint, there was an ulcer measuring 4.5 x 2.3 cm; on the left ankle joint's anterior-medial surface, an ulcer measuring 3 x 4 cm. Treatment: 25 sessions. Primarily, the emitter was applied to the ulcer area. Result: The ulcer healed well, and the swelling noticeably decreased, allowing the patient to stand and walk for longer periods. The feeling of discomfort in the legs was almost imperceptible, and there were no restrictions on standing time. After 25 sessions : The size of the right ulcer reduced to 1.4 x 1.0 cm, the left ulcer was completely epithelialized. Treatment continued once a week for a month until full recovery. Side Effects : None. Comments : The ZB emitter mainly affects the normalization of the condition of blood vessels by removing pathological collagen from their walls.

Patient: Born in 1982, admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis - Dermatomyositis, Polymyositis, Act II, Stage II. From the medical history, she has been ill since March 1996 when she first noticed skin thickening on the face, neck, arms, legs, and abdomen. She underwent hormonal therapy for 1.5 years. Objectively, skin thickening is noted on the neck, arms, shoulders, forearms, back, abdomen, thighs, and calves (more on the right and extensor surfaces). Her weight is 84 kg with a height of 148 cm. Treatment lasted for 3.5 months, receiving ZB for 5-15 minutes 2 times a week, RC with a floating schedule + KL for 15 minutes daily, GI(s) on the intestines for 15-20 minutes and on the kidneys for 5 minutes for one month, KL(s) on the thymus and pancreas for 2 months. As a result of the therapy, skin thickening disappeared, skin color normalized, skin turgor was preserved, hormonal drugs were no longer taken, and weight decreased to 60 kg.

Patient: 12 years old. Diagnosed with autism at age 2. Main symptoms: Does not control anger, scattered attention, sluggishness, weak communication skills. Born a normal child with no birth complications. Development was normal until age 2, then unusual behavior was noticed when she stopped responding to external stimuli. The patient underwent courses of physiotherapy and acupuncture. Her mother, a teacher, devoted much time to her development. At age 9, there was some improvement; she could write, read, and use a computer. Understands TV programs and spoken language, speaks English and Malay well, can answer questions. However, her attention span is very short, easily irritated when a question is repeated if she hasn't answered yet. Usually screams in response. Typically can only read 3-4 sentences and does not focus on continuing. A 10-day daily RT course was conducted. Progress Noted: Based on parental observation, the patient usually can concentrate on just a few sentences. After 5 days of therapy, she was able to concentrate longer, and after 10 days, she could read 3-4 pages at once. Surprisingly, by the end of the course, she could lie calmly on the bed for a 2-hour treatment session, although in the first days, she couldn't sit or lie still. She also became less aggressive, and according to her parents, less easily irritated than before treatment. Side Effect : During treatment, after the first sessions, the patient developed itchy spots. The rash appeared suddenly and disappeared on its own without medication. Comments: Improvement in concentration after the resonance therapy course. Unfortunately, a longer therapy course was not possible due to demographic reasons.

Patient: 60 years old, has had diabetes for 15 years, concerned about deteriorating vision, numbness in feet and hands. There's an infiltrate on the right big toe with marked hyperemia, swelling, and a central necrosis focus, but no pain in the infiltrate area. Drainage was performed, expelling 10 ml of pus. The patient was treated with RT using GI, ZB, and KL emitters. As a result of treatment, the wound healed, sensitivity in the lower extremities significantly improved, the numbness in the toes was reduced by 90% compared to the initial state. An interesting observation was that after 3 weeks of treatment, the patient's vision improved. (She started reading again, although she hadn't been able to do so for nearly 8 years). No side effects were observed.

A 54-year-old female patient has had diabetes for over 10 years and has been taking oral hypoglycemic medications. A month ago, a trophic ulcer appeared on the first toe of the foot, which progressed to gangrene with inflammation of the subcutaneous fat tissue around the periphery. The surgeon proposed an operation to remove the entire foot, and possibly, if circulation in the lower leg was poor, amputation up to the popliteal fossa. The patient categorically refused the operation. Treatment with infrared (IR) emitters was initiated. The affected limb was treated with GI and RV emitters for 10–20 minutes twice a day. On the third day of treatment, ZB was added for 3–5 minutes on the affected area and 10 minutes twice a day on the lower leg. Additionally, KL-s emitters were applied to the pancreas for 5 minutes in two projections. As a result of the therapy, the patient began experiencing pain (before treatment, she had no sensation in the affected limb), and the signs of inflammation around the gangrene focus significantly decreased. Amputation was limited to the gangrenous area, as circulation in the leg and foot vessels remained normal. No side effects were observed. Comments: For all patients with diabetic foot lesions, GI and ZB emitters are used (GI destroys pathogenic bacteria, while ZB improves microcirculation). Treatment should begin as early as possible, increasing exposure to 40–60 minutes three to four times a day. If the clinical picture is favorable, surgical intervention can be postponed. Standard wound care and surgical removal of necrotic tissue are performed.

Patient Z.A., a 60-year-old woman, has had diabetes for 15 years, with worsening vision, peripheral neuropathy, and numbness in her legs and hands. She also had an infiltrate with pronounced hyperemia, swelling, and a necrotic center on the big toe of her right foot, but no pain in the area. Drainage was performed, releasing 10 ml of pus. The patient was treated with IR therapy, mainly using GI, ZB, and KL emitters. Result: The wound healed, and sensitivity in the lower limbs improved significantly. Numbness in her toes decreased by 90% compared to the initial state. An interesting observation was that after three weeks, her vision improved. The patient could read, something she had been unable to do for almost eight years before therapy. No side effects were observed. Comments: The ZB emitter is recommended for diabetic retinopathy treatment. Since it is effective in treating diabetic retinopathy, it may also be used for its prevention. Therapy is very simple—only 1 minute, two to three times a day, and possibly once daily for preventive purposes.

Patient B.Y., a 60-year-old man, has had hypertension and diabetes for 30 years. His vision was weak, and he could not read. His blood pressure (BP) had been poorly controlled for 30 years, usually ranging from 150/100 to 170/110. When he visited the Infra Life clinic, his BP remained at 160–170/110 despite taking maximum doses of prazosin, nifedipine, and enalapril. His diastolic pressure had never been below 90 mmHg in the last 20 years. He also took high doses of glibenclamide and metformin for diabetes. He underwent a course of resonance IR therapy using GI, ZB, KL, and AK emitters. Result: His BP significantly decreased and stabilized at 130/70. Prazosin was discontinued, and the doses of the other two antihypertensive drugs were halved. His BP remained stable at 130/80 in the morning, sometimes reaching 120–130/70. His vision improved remarkably—he could read the Quran and newspapers. Peripheral neuropathy in his toes improved by 90% compared to the initial state. He lost 9 kg through diet. His physical condition improved, and he could walk for half an hour without fatigue. No side effects were observed. The improvement in physical condition and weight loss were considered positive side effects, commonly seen in most patients. Comments: The ZB emitter can be used to treat diabetic retinopathy. Since it is effective for treating diabetic retinopathy, it may also be recommended for prevention. The therapy is simple—just 1 minute, two to three times a day, or possibly once daily for prevention. In 35 out of 40 patients, BP stabilization was observed. Dose reduction or discontinuation of medications was also an interesting phenomenon. However, the question of how to maintain BP using IR emitters remains under study.

A 41-year-old male patient had diabetes for many years and was taking Glucophage and glibenclamide tablets. Complaints : A painless, non-healing ulcer the size of a coin on the right sole for two years, along with symptoms of diabetic neuropathy. The ulcer had remained the same size for two years. The patient underwent debridement and surgical cleaning of necrotic tissue, which led to noticeable healing but not complete closure. The wound remained open. Suturing was attempted, but fluid continued to ooze from the wound. The wound was cleaned daily with a standard saline solution. It remained clean, but its edges were thickened, and the size did not change. An orthopedic surgeon performed a Z-shaped incision and sutured the ulcer. Simultaneously, resonance therapy was initiated. The ulcer completely healed within two weeks. After another two weeks, numbness and reduced sensitivity in his toes improved, though some residual numbness remained. Treatment was discontinued because the patient lived far away and could not attend sessions regularly. His overall condition also significantly improved. No side effects were observed. Comments: The effects of IR therapy on diabetic foot lesions have been noted in many patients undergoing this treatment. The therapy improves blood circulation in the lower limbs.

A 50-year-old male patient has suffered from constant diplopia for 5 years, sometimes so severe that he is unable to drive. He takes pyridostigmine regularly. Additionally, he has a 5×6 cm lipoma on the right side of his head and experiences elevated blood pressure (160-170/100-110) despite taking antihypertensive medication. A course of infrared therapy ("INFRA R") was administered, with the primary emitter applied to the eye area (GI), selected based on EAF (electro-acupuncture feedback) indicators. The treatment was conducted six days a week for four weeks, followed by continued home therapy using GI and ZB emitters. The patient visits for follow-up every two weeks. Result: Within two months of treatment initiation, diplopia did not recur. Blood pressure slightly decreased, stabilizing at 140-150/90-100, and medication intake was reduced to once daily.

A 51-year-old male patient was advised by his ophthalmologist to undergo urgent surgery in Australia. Instead, he sought a trial course of infrared therapy ("INFRA R") at Infra Life Clinic. During the therapy, he continued weekly ophthalmologist visits to monitor the response. The newly formed blood vessels constricted to the point of becoming undetectable, and the cornea returned to a completely normal state. Additionally, all his gray hair turned black. He also had suffered from tinnitus for 20 years due to a bomb explosion during military service. After therapy, the tinnitus disappeared.

A male patient, born in 1950, was admitted with a diagnosis of intestinal dysbacteriosis. Complaints included frequent bowel movements with undigested food after every meal and significant weight loss. The condition had persisted for two years, and previous medical treatments provided only temporary relief. At admission : Bodyweight deficit of 21% (height 188 cm, weight <70 kg), pale skin, reduced skin turgor, fatigue, and weakness. Treatment : GI(s) emitter applied to the intestinal area for 15 minutes GI “CT” for 20 minutes GI(b)+KL according to the general treatment schedule for 1 week Results : Normalized stool after the first session; improved energy levels after the fifth session. The patient completed a two-week course. One-year follow-up showed no recurrence of intestinal disorders, and the patient gained 14 kg.

sections.title: CALF MUSCLE DISCOMFORT AND DROWSINESS
paragraphs: A 40-year-old male teacher complained of persistent drowsiness and calf muscle discomfort for two years. He attributed the muscle discomfort to prolonged standing at work. The pain was most noticeable in the morning and evening. Examination revealed tenderness upon palpation of the calf muscle; arterial pulsation was normal. Treatment : GI and ZB emitters applied to the calf muscle. Results : Daily noticeable improvement; discomfort completely resolved after three sessions. Drowsiness was noted only after the first session. The patient felt more energetic, and sleepiness disappeared. Since the improvement occurred within three days, treatment was discontinued. Comments : Similar therapy has shown good results in other patients with similar conditions.

Patient F.Y., a 27-year-old male, was involved in a car accident four months before treatment, sustaining a mid-shaft fracture of the right femur. Two months post-injury, there was no bone union and only minimal callus formation. A bone graft was performed. After four months, callus formation was observed, but not at the fracture site. The patient was using crutches and unable to lift anything. EAF indicators ranged between 70-85 at most points. Therapy was primarily conducted using RC, RV, GI, ZB, and KB emitters. The RV emitter elicited a response, but morning therapy sessions showed unchanged EAF levels. Results : X-ray after three weeks showed increased callus formation. After six weeks, a well-formed callus was observed, and the patient was able to walk without crutches. No side effects were noted. Comments : During the first week, EAF indicators showed no response to the KB emitter, which is typically used for osteogenesis. This suggests that the delayed healing was not solely due to the fracture itself but also systemic dysfunction, as indicated by the EAF readings.

A 55-year-old patient complained of constipation for 3-5 days, pain along the colon. According to EAF, numbers below the norm of 35-40 were noted at the colon points and bac nodules were tested. Salmonella. The improvement of the indicators was observed with the use of the GI emitter. Normalization of stool in the patient was noted after 6 procedures.

A 75-year-old male patient complained of difficulty urinating and frequent nighttime urination (4-5 times per night). Ultrasound confirmed prostate adenoma.
