Treatment: "CT" device and simultaneous application of RC emitter to the abdominal wall, followed by ZB+KL emitters GI+ZB emitters applied to the intestines KL emitter applied to the thymus, heels, pancreas, and hypothalamus Results : By the third day, urination became easier. After seven days, nighttime urination reduced to 1-2 times per night. After 10 days, only once per night. A follow-up ultrasound showed a 20% reduction in prostate size.

Patient H.S., an 80-year-old female, had been diagnosed with CAD seven years prior and had hypertension for 15 years. Unable to tolerate any medications due to adverse effects. At the time of admission, she was bedridden, experiencing severe chest pain and shortness of breath with minimal movement. For the past 3-4 years, she had up to 20 pain episodes daily. Treatment : 30-day infrared therapy, using ZB, AK, and GI emitters on the heart and affected organs. Initial blood pressure: 160-170/100-110. Results : By day 3, fewer chest pain episodes, with no severe nighttime attacks. After two weeks, pain was infrequent and milder. Blood pressure stabilized at 150-160/80-90. After one month, she continued home therapy with GI and ZB emitters. Her condition remained stable with no side effects.

A male patient, born in 1956, was admitted with severe IDDM, lower limb angiopathy, and retinopathy. Comorbidities included cervical-thoracic osteochondrosis and chronic cholecystitis. History : Diagnosed 18 years ago, onset linked to severe stress, initially presenting as a diabetic coma. Requires 56 units of insulin daily. Complaints : Dry mouth, significant weight loss, leg pain and numbness, drowsiness, and constipation. Treatment : Comprehensive infrared therapy over 12 days. Results : By day 3, dry mouth disappeared. By day 8, numbness and leg cramps resolved. By day 10, lower limb pulse became detectable. By day 12, he gained 2 kg. Lab tests normalized, and insulin dosage was reduced from 56 to 36 units daily. A one-year follow-up showed further insulin reduction to 13 units/day.

A female patient, born in 1925, was admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of severe insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM) with weight loss, complicated by a trophic ulcer on the right foot and diabetic nephropathy. Comorbid pathology: cerebral atherosclerosis. Complaints: Severe pain in the right leg, leg swelling, non-healing ulcer on the right foot, thirst, severe weakness, dizziness, and hand tremors. Medical history: Diagnosed with diabetes for 20 years, but has been taking insulin only for the past 5 years at a daily dose of 32 units (four times a day: 8-10-8-6). The patient has received both inpatient and outpatient treatment multiple times and has undergone three surgeries for a non-healing trophic ulcer on the right foot (ulcer since 1996). Objective data: General condition: severe. Pale skin and visible mucous membranes, pasty face. Heart sounds muffled, accentuated second heart sound over the aorta. Blood pressure: 140/100 mmHg. The abdomen is bloated and slightly tense (flatulence). Pasternatsky's symptom is weakly positive on both sides. Leg swelling present. Postoperative wound on the right foot measuring 20x12 cm with smooth edges, discharging serous-purulent fluid. Laboratory and instrumental findings: CBC: RBC – 3.9, WBC – 9.2, lymphocytes – 44%, ESR – 22 mm/h. Blood glucose: 12 mmol/L, Urine glucose: 3%. ECG: pronounced dystrophic changes in the myocardium, left ventricular hypertrophy. Fundus examination: phonosclerosis, retinal vessel angiopathy, narrowed arteries, tortuous veins, thrombosis of small venous vessels, visual acuity: OD/OS 0.6/0.6. Electroacupuncture findings: Decreased indicators on biologically active points (BAPs) of the lymphatic system, lungs, large intestine, and nervous system. Sharply reduced indicators on the meridians of blood vessels, pancreas, spleen, stomach, and bladder. High readings on kidney and gallbladder meridians. Treatment (34 days): GI therapy: general, starting with 20 minutes and increasing daily to 40 minutes for 18 days. RC therapy: general, increasing from 1.5x2 min to 3x2 min over 16 days. AF therapy: general, 10-15 minutes. KL therapy: local (heels: 5-20 min, pancreas: 5 min in two projections). ZB therapy: general, 10 min once a week. Results: The trophic ulcer on the right foot healed. Insulin dose reduced to 13 units/day (three doses: 4-5-4). Blood glucose decreased to 7.2 mmol/L, urine glucose absent. CBC: Hb – 102 g/L, RBC – 4.2, WBC – 6.8, ESR – 16 mm/h. Fundus examination: retinal angiopathy, moderate vein dilation and tortuosity, isolated microaneurysms, visual acuity: OD/OS 0.8/0.8. Electroacupuncture indicators normalized. Clinical Observations: The clinic monitored 151 diabetic patients, including 18 with insulin-dependent diabetes (IDDM) and 133 with non-insulin-dependent diabetes (NIDDM). Patients ranged in age from 12 to 75 years, with disease duration from newly diagnosed (4.6%) to 25 years. Despite prior therapy, all patients had elevated blood sugar levels (8.2 to 20.8 mmol/L), diabetic neuropathy, and micro/macroangiopathy (retinopathy, nephropathy – 84.6%). Non-healing trophic ulcers were observed in 10.6%, gangrene of the foot in 4%, fungal infections in 8%, and 5 male patients reported impotence. Average blood glucose levels: IDDM – 12.9±2.9 mmol/L, NIDDM – 10.9±3.2 mmol/L. Daily insulin dose before treatment: 20 to 60 units. Most NIDDM patients: on oral hypoglycemic drugs. Infrared Therapy Approach: Infrared (IR) therapy was used to provide anti-inflammatory effects, improve microcirculation, and normalize immune function. The type of IR emitter was selected via electroacupuncture findings (EAF). Daily procedures included: Regulation of the autonomic nervous system and pancreatic function Metabolic normalization Treatment of chronic infections Microcirculation improvement Treatment Outcomes: Duration: 12-24 days Patient response: Significant improvement by day 7-8 Thirst and dry mouth disappeared Increased energy and work capacity By week 2, stabilized blood glucose: NIDDM: 5.2±2.8 mmol/L, IDDM: 8.45±2.4 mmol/L Angiopathy and neuropathy symptoms resolved in 4.6% of patients, significantly reduced in others 100% healing of trophic ulcers Gangrene cases: reduced need for surgery Fungal infections: completely treated Impotence: significant improvement NIDDM patients: many stopped or reduced oral medication IDDM patients: 6 patients reduced insulin dose by 10±5 units/day

A 40-year-old female patient with IDDM, taking 50 units of insulin twice daily for the past 5 years. Blood glucose fluctuated between 8-12 mmol/L, sometimes rising to 14-16 mmol/L. Hospitalized for tonsillitis with high glucose (14-16 mmol/L) despite usual insulin dose. Treatment: Resonance IR therapy daily for 7 days, then irregularly (once every 2-3 days due to work schedule). Results: Pre-insulin blood glucose stabilized at 4-6 mmol/L Insulin dose reduced to 30 units/day Continued irregular IR therapy (once or twice weekly) No side effects observed Comments: Resonance therapy is effective for both Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes. Many patients achieve significant improvement or discontinue medications entirely, but full success requires 2-3 months of treatment, which most patients are unwilling to commit to. Practice in Tashkent confirms that insulin doses can be significantly reduced.

A female patient, born in 1970, was diagnosed with mild, slow-progressing NIDDM upon hospital admission. Comorbid condition: Chronic cholecystitis (exacerbated). Complaints: Pain in the right hypochondrium, thirst, dry mouth, headaches, and constipation (bowel movement every 2-3 days). Medical history: Family history of diabetes (maternal side) Self-reported symptoms for 1 year, associated with overwork No prior treatment Objective data: General condition: relatively satisfactory Weight: normal Skin: pale Tongue: coated yellow at the root Abdomen: tender in the right/left hypochondrium Liver: palpable, tender, smooth surface Lab results: Blood glucose: 7.2 mmol/L Urine glucose: 0.3% Prothrombin index (PTI): 98% Treatment (2 weeks): GI therapy: 20-40 min daily Local therapy: liver, intestines, adrenals, kidneys, spine (5 min daily) ZB therapy: 10 min, twice weekly Results: After 1 week: symptom relief After 2 weeks: blood glucose 4.8 mmol/L, urine glucose absent Follow-up after 1 month: Blood glucose 5.2 mmol/L

The patient, born in 1947, was admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, moderate course, complicated by angiopathy of the lower limb vessels, retinopathy, and nephropathy. Comorbid conditions include chronic colitis and hemorrhoids. Complaints upon admission: dry mouth, weakness, quick fatigue, sweating, itching, cold extremities, discomfort in the pancreas area, slow wound healing, constipation. History : The patient has been ill for 2 years, with the onset of the disease associated with stress. Previous treatment: diet, taking Maninil 1 tablet twice a day for the last 3-4 months. No effect from therapy, and the disease is progressing. Objective data : General condition is relatively satisfactory, body weight exceeds normal by 20%. Skin is pale with an earthy hue, rash under the breasts and around the genitals. The spine is tender to palpation in the lumbar area, knee and ankle joints are painful, the face is swollen, eyelids are puffy. Blood pressure is 130/80. The tongue is coated with a white film at the root. Abdomen is tender to palpation in the left hypochondrium and around the navel. The liver protrudes 0.5 cm below the costal margin, painless on palpation, medium density, sharp edge, smooth surface. Pain is noted on palpation of the pancreas. The Pasternack's sign is positive on both sides. Urination is free but frequent, with nocturia, polyuria, and incontinence. Laboratory-instrumental tests : blood sugar 9.2, urine sugar 1%, fibrinogen 2.42, PTI 100, ultrasound – pancreas contours are smooth, unclear, echostructure is homogeneous, the gland is diffusely thickened, dimensions 2.6 x 1.3 x 2.4. EAF data: Pancreas meridian: protein metabolism temperature 15, nucleoprotein synthesis temperature 87, pancreas duct temperature 72, carbohydrate enzyme synthesis temperature 41, KT 49; indicators on the vascular system meridian range from 69-71, nerve system meridian: parasympathetic ganglion temperature on the left 22; allergy meridian control point on the right 33, left 14, endocrine system meridian control point on the right 70, left 31. Treatment : KL locally on the pancreas area before and after treatment for 5 minutes, twice a day for 3 weeks; GI general for 15 to 30 minutes for 2 weeks; GI + ZB locally on the liver, adrenal glands, intestines, spine, pancreas for 3-5 minutes for 3 weeks; ZB general for 5-7-10 minutes every 2 days starting from the 2nd week of treatment. Treatment specifics : During therapy, intravenous Reopolyglukin solution was used once. The Maninil dosage was reduced by half (0.5 tablet twice a day) by the end of the 2nd week, and Maninil tablets were completely discontinued by the end of the 3rd week. Result: After one week of therapy, the patient’s overall condition improved, blood pressure normalized, the tongue was cleared of the coating, urination and stool normalized, urine sugar was 0.5%, joint pain disappeared after 2 weeks, abdominal palpation became painless, liver was no longer palpable, Pasternack’s sign negative on both sides, blood sugar decreased to 7.8 mmol/l. By the end of the 3rd week, body weight decreased by 5%, skin cleared, lumbar spine pain disappeared, and swelling reduced. On ultrasound, the pancreas contour was clear, the echostructure was homogeneous, and the size was 2.5 x 1.3 x 2.4. EAF parameters normalized. Blood sugar was 5.2 mmol/l, urine sugar absent, fibrinogen 2.02, PTI 89.

The patient, born in 1950, was admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, slowly progressing severe course, complicated by diabetic nephropathy. Comorbid pathology includes chronic cholecystitis in the acute stage, chronic pyelonephritis in remission. Complaints upon admission : quick fatigue, thirst, frequent headaches, periodic increases in blood pressure up to 180/100, urinary incontinence, unpleasant odor in the urine, low back pain. History : Family history is not burdened. The patient has been ill for 2 years and associates the onset of the disease with a previous acute viral infection. No specific anti-diabetic therapy was provided, the patient took high doses of vitamin C. Objective data : General condition is relatively satisfactory, skin is pale with an earthy hue, spine is deformed, pronounced scoliosis LIII – LIV, kyphosis TIII – DV, spine is painful on palpation in the lumbar area, pronounced swelling of the lower limbs, face, and eyelids, expiratory shortness of breath, respiratory rate 16, pulse 98 bpm, blood pressure 150/100, tongue is coated with a yellow film. Abdomen is tender on palpation in the right and left hypochondria. The liver is palpable, tender, protruding 2-3 cm from the costal margin, of medium density, smooth surface, rounded edge. Pasternack’s sign is markedly positive on both sides. Urination is painful, frequent, polyuria, stool is constipated (once every 3-4 days). Laboratory-instrumental studies : blood sugar 9.8 mmol/l, urine sugar 0.7%, eye fundus – angiopathy of retinal vessels, arterial narrowing, increased venous tortuosity. EAF indicators : on the vascular system, nervous system, and pancreas meridians, all indicators are decreased (20-30). Treatment: GI general according to the schedule once a day, daily for 3 weeks, GI + ZB locally on the liver, gallbladder, kidneys, spine, ovaries, uterus, perineum, intestines for 5 minutes once a day, daily for 3 weeks. RC+ZB locally on the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spine, ovaries, uterus, perineum, intestines, head for 2 minutes once a day, daily for 3 weeks, ZB general for 5 minutes once a day for 3 weeks, KL general for 10 minutes once a day for 3 weeks, locally on the heels for 15 minutes, pancreas 5x5 minutes twice a day before and after treatment, 1 minute on the occiput, 2 minutes on the thymus, 5 minutes on the intestines. Stool RC + KL for 10-15 minutes. Therapy specifics : On the 4th day of therapy, the body temperature rose to 39°C and remained for 2 days. Hemodez solution 400 ml was used intravenously once during therapy. Result : After 1 week of therapy, the overall condition improved, fatigue and thirst disappeared, blood pressure normalized, blood sugar was 8.4 mmol/l, urine sugar 0.5%. After 2 weeks, low back pain disappeared, urination normalized, skin regained its normal color, edema and shortness of breath disappeared, blood sugar decreased to 7.2 mmol/l. By the end of the 3rd week, all EAF parameters normalized, scoliosis decreased, blood sugar was 5.2 mmol/l, urine sugar absent, eye fundus – retinal vessel angiopathy, moderate venous dilatation, slight irregularity of their caliber.

The patient, born in 1963, was admitted to the clinic with newly diagnosed rapidly progressing Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, complicated by retinopathy. Comorbid pathology includes chronic hepatitis in the acute stage, chronic cholecystitis, hypertensive disease stage II-A, chronic cystitis in the acute stage. Complaints : purulent rashes all over the body and face, poor wound healing, burns over the last 2 years, occasional increases in blood pressure, vision loss, temperature rise up to 37.5°C. History : Family history is burdened on the maternal side, the patient considers herself ill for 2 years, associates the onset of the disease with a previous hepatitis. Previous treatment: Essentiale-forte, antibiotics, general strengthening therapy, antispasmodics. Objective data : General condition is relatively satisfactory, skin is yellowish, spine is deformed, kyphosis TIII-TIV, painful on palpation in the lumbar area, lower limbs are swollen, inspiratory shortness of breath with increased blood pressure, blood pressure 180/110, tongue coated with yellow film. Abdomen is tender to palpation in the epigastric region, right and left hypochondria, the liver protrudes from the costal margin by 3-4 cm, painful on palpation, medium density, smooth surface, sharp edge. Painful urination, frequent, polyuria. Laboratory-instrumental studies : Blood sugar 10 mmol/l, urine sugar 0.7%. Eye fundus – angiopathy of retinal vessels, arteries narrowed, veins tortuous, uneven caliber. Visual acuity OD/OS — 0.9/0.8. EAF indicators decreased on all meridians (12-34), pancreas meridian (5-24). Treatment was conducted once a day, daily for 2 weeks : GI general according to the schedule, locally for all zones for 5 minutes; RC general according to the schedule, locally on the head, spine, pancreas, gallbladder for 2 minutes, ZB general for 5 minutes, locally for all zones for 3 minutes, KL general for 10 minutes, locally on the pancreas 5x5 minutes twice a day before and after treatment, head 1 minute, spine 2 minutes, heels 15 minutes, thymus 2 minutes. Therapy specifics : By the end of the first week of therapy, a paronychia developed on the foot, which resolved within 8 days (drainage phenomenon). Results: By the end of the first week of therapy, the overall condition improved, skin regained its normal color, blood pressure normalized (120/80), body temperature normalized, urination improved, blood sugar was 8.9 mmol/l, urine sugar 0.3%. After 2 weeks, purulent rashes disappeared, kyphotic spinal curvature was corrected, swelling disappeared, abdomen was painless on palpation, liver was non-palpable, protruding 0.5-2 cm from the costal margin, blood sugar was 5.6 mmol/l, urine sugar absent, eye fundus – diabetic retinal angiopathy, moderate venous dilation, slight unevenness of their caliber, Vis OD/OS – 1.0/1.0. EAF parameters normalized.

Patient, born 1972, upon admission to the clinic, was diagnosed with slowly progressing NIDDM, mild course. Comorbidities include chronic hepatitis in the exacerbation stage, chronic colitis. Complaints : Dry mouth, weakness, headaches, sleep disturbances, pain in the left hypochondrium. History : Family history burdened on both maternal and paternal sides. Considers herself ill for 2 years, associates the onset with hepatitis. Previously treated for hepatitis. Objective Data : General condition relatively satisfactory. Skin jaundiced, lower limb edema, tongue coated with yellow, pharynx and tonsils hyperemic, hypertrophied. Abdomen painful on palpation in the epigastric area, right and left hypochondrium. Liver protrudes 3-4 cm below the costal margin, painful on palpation, medium density, smooth surface, sharp edge. Pasternatsky's sign positive bilaterally, frequent urination, polyuria, bowel movement once every 3-4 days. Laboratory Tests : Blood sugar 8.4 mmol/L, urine sugar 0.75%. Prothrombin time index (PTI) 100. Treatment: General GI for 20-40 minutes once a day, daily for 2 weeks, local GI + ZB on liver, kidneys, spine, intestine, pancreas for 5 minutes once a day for 2 weeks. General RC twice a week for 7 minutes, locally on liver, pancreas, kidneys, intestine, head, ovaries, uterus for 2 minutes, thymus 1 minute once a day for 2 weeks, general ZB twice a week for 10 minutes for 2 weeks, locally on liver, kidney, intestine, pancreas for 10 minutes, head for 1 minute once a day for 2 weeks. General KL for 10 minutes every other day for 2 weeks, locally on heels for 20 minutes, pancreas 5x5 minutes twice a day before and after treatment, 1 minute on the nape. Course of Therapy : Diarrhea appeared on the 3rd day of therapy, lasting for 4 days (drainage). Results : After 1 week of therapy, the general condition improved, skin color normalized, tongue cleared of coating, pharynx calm, urination and bowel movements normalized. By the end of the 2nd week of treatment, edema disappeared, abdomen painless on palpation, liver not palpable, Pasternatsky's sign negative bilaterally. Blood sugar 4.8 mmol/L, no sugar in urine. PTI 86.

sections.title: NON-INSULIN DEPENDENT DIABETES MELLITUS
paragraphs: Patient, born 1964, upon admission to the clinic, diagnosed with NIDDM, mild, slowly progressing course. Comorbidities: chronic cystitis in the exacerbation stage, uterine fibroids - 3-4 weeks, right-sided hearing loss. Complaints : Quick fatigue, thirst, severe headaches, urinary incontinence, lower back pain, constipation. History : Considers herself ill for 2 years, links the onset to a cold. Objective Data : General condition relatively satisfactory. Weight exceeds norm by 20%, skin pale, rash around genitals, spine curved, kyphosis TIII-TIV painful on palpation in the lumbar area, edema of lower limbs and face, BP 140/100. Abdomen painful on palpation in the epigastric area, right and left hypochondrium. Liver protrudes 0.5 cm below the costal margin, painless on palpation, medium density, smooth surface, sharp edge. Pasternatsky's sign positive bilaterally, painful urination, frequent, polyuria. Indicators on all meridians by EAF reduced (on endocrine system and pancreas meridians from 5 to 38, only the carbohydrate metabolism point at 85). Laboratory Tests: Blood sugar 7.2 mmol/L, urine sugar 0.5%, PTI 98. Treatment : General GI once a day for 2 weeks, local GI + ZB on liver, kidneys, spine, pancreas, intestine for 5 minutes once a day for 2 weeks; ZB twice a week for 10 minutes, locally on head for 5-7 minutes once a day for 2 weeks; General KL for 10 minutes once a day for 2 weeks, locally on heels, pancreas, thymus for 5 minutes, head for 1 minute, bladder for 5-10 minutes. Sitz bath (RC+ZC) on uterus and bladder - 10 minutes. Results : By the end of the 1st week of therapy, general condition improved, skin around genitals cleared of rash, BP normalized to 120/80, abdomen painless on palpation, liver not palpable. By the end of the 2nd week of treatment, kyphotic spinal curvature disappeared, edema gone, Pasternatsky's sign negative. Blood sugar 5.4 mmol/L, no sugar in urine, PTI 84. EAF indicators normalized.

Patient, born 1947, admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of slowly progressing NIDDM, moderate severity, complicated by diabetic nephropathy. Comorbidities: chronic cholecystitis in the exacerbation stage, chronic pyelonephritis in the exacerbation stage. Complaints : Dry mouth, lower back pain, severe headaches, constipation. History : Family history burdened on the maternal side. Ill for 3 years, does not associate the onset with any event. Treated both as an outpatient and inpatient, takes Glurenorm 1/2 tablet twice a day, diuretics, with temporary improvements. Objective Data : General condition relatively satisfactory. Weight exceeds norm by 10%, skin pale with an earthy tint. Spine painful on palpation in the lumbar area. Facial and lower limb edema. Expiratory dyspnea. BP 140/100. Tongue coated yellow, tonsils hypertrophied, abdomen painful on palpation in the epigastric area, right and left hypochondrium. Liver protrudes 1 cm below the costal margin, painful on palpation, medium density, smooth surface, sharp edge. Pasternatsky's sign positive bilaterally, painful, frequent urination, polyuria. Laboratory Data : Blood sugar 7.8 mmol/L, urine sugar 2%, PTI 100. EAF Indicators : On the pancreas meridian, protein metabolism point 18, carbohydrate enzyme synthesis 72, nucleoprotein synthesis 84, on points of endocrine system and blood vessels meridians, indicators within 30-40. Treatment : General GI for 15-40 minutes once a day for 2 weeks, local GI + ZB on liver, kidneys, spine, intestine for 5 minutes once a day for 2 weeks; General ZB for 3-5-7-10 minutes once a day for 2 weeks, locally on head for 3-5 minutes once a day for 2 weeks; General KL for 10 minutes once a day for 2 weeks, locally on heels for 10-20 minutes, pancreas 5x5 minutes, 7th cervical vertebra for 2 minutes, head for 1 minute once a day for 2 weeks. Course of Therapy : Diarrhea on the 3rd day of therapy, lasting 4 days with the passage of fecal stones. Results : By the end of the 1st week of therapy, the general condition improved, skin color normalized, spine painless on palpation, BP 120/90, tongue clean, tonsils of normal size. By the end of the 2nd week, edema and dyspnea disappeared, abdomen painless on palpation, liver not palpable, Pasternatsky's sign negative. Blood sugar 5.0 mmol/L, no sugar in urine, PTI 92. All EAF indicators normalized. In the middle of the 2nd week of treatment, the patient stopped taking Glurenorm, tolerating the discontinuation well.

Patient, born 1948, admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of NIDDM, moderate-severe form, with weight loss, complicated by macroangiopathy. Comorbidities: atherosclerosis, chronic prostatitis in the exacerbation stage, chronic calculous cholecystitis in the exacerbation stage. Complaints : Periodically dry mouth, weakness, sweating, frequent urination, especially at night, pain in the right hypochondrium. History : Ill for 6 years, takes Buckarban 1/2 tablet, increases to 1 tablet daily when blood sugar rises. Objective Data : General condition relatively satisfactory. Abdomen painful on palpation in the right hypochondrium, liver not enlarged. Pulsation of leg vessels weakened. Laboratory-Instrumental Tests : CBC: Hb-142 g/L, Erythrocytes 4.1, Leukocytes – 4.8, ESR 8 mm/hr. Neutrophils segmented 61, band 5, lymphocytes 31, monocytes 1. UA: Protein 0.033%, urine sugar 2%, pH 6.0. Blood sugar 16 mmol/L. Ultrasound - signs of chronic calculous cholecystitis, prostatic hyperplasia. REG - blood filling of leg vessels reduced, more on the left. EAF Indicators : on points of all meridians elevated to 80-92. Treatment : General KL for 10 minutes once a week. Local on pancreas, heels for 5-20 minutes once a day, daily, daily CNS state regulation. General RC 10-14-20-40 minutes daily, locally on liver, kidneys, prostate, spine, General GI 20-30-40-50 minutes daily, locally on intestine, lungs, spine, pancreas. General ZC for 20 minutes daily, locally on pancreas, prostate for 10 minutes each. Course of Therapy : Single intravenous drip infusion of Hemodez 200 ml. Results : Improvement of general condition noted on the 3rd day of therapy, right hypochondrium pain relieved on the 6th day, normalization of urination on the 10th day. After 1 month post-treatment, completely stopped taking antidiabetic medication, pulsation of leg vessels satisfactory. CBC and UA normalized. Blood sugar 8.2 mmol/L, urine sugar 0.5%. Ultrasound - signs of chronic calculous cholecystitis, chronic prostatitis. REG - blood filling of leg vessels satisfactory. Indicators on points of all meridians 76-82.

Patient, born 1933, admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of NIDDM, moderate severity, complicated by macroangiopathy, polyneuropathy, gangrene of the right foot. Comorbidities: cerebral atherosclerosis, hypertension, osteoarthritis of the knee joints, chronic cholecystitis in remission, chronic pyelonephritis. Complaints: General weakness, quick fatigue, drowsiness, dry mouth with bitterness, urinary incontinence, itching in the perineum, heart pain, headaches, dizziness, periodic blood pressure rises up to 180/100, constantly cold feet. History : Ill for 12 years, disease detected during a medical check-up. Takes Glurenorm 1 tablet 2-3 times a day. Objective Data : General condition relatively satisfactory. Tongue coated white, swollen, bad breath. Heart sounds muffled, accentuated second sound on the aorta. Liver enlarged due to the right lobe +5-6 cm, painless, slight pain on palpation of the bladder. On the right foot's little toe, there's a wound 1.5x2 cm with a black scab, surrounded by infiltrative edema, painful on palpation, pulsation of leg vessels reduced, feet cold to touch. Laboratory-Instrumental Tests : CBC: Hb – 159 g/L, Erythrocytes – 4.6, Leukocytes – 4.0, band neutrophils 3, segmented 63, lymphocytes 24, monocytes 2, eosinophils 8, ESR 5 mm/hr. Blood sugar 11.0 mmol/L, PTI 89, urine sugar 1%. Coagulogram – hypercoagulation, REG - reduced blood filling of leg arteries, normal tone. Ultrasound liver +0.5 cm on the right +7 cm, gallbladder unevenly thickened, contents not visualized. Fundus examination – angiosclerosis, retinal angiopathy. Treatment : Conducted over 1 month: daily CNS state regulation with KL and KH, first 4 days: general RV+ZC for 20-25 minutes for 4 days, local RC on pancreas, adrenals, vascular bundle, lungs, kidneys, liver, intestine for 2-5 minutes, AK on eyes 2-2-2 minutes twice a day before and after treatment, local KL on pancreas 5x5 minutes, heels 20 minutes once a day; next 6 days: general GI+RC+ZB for 25-30 minutes once a day, local GI on intestine, pancreas, kidneys, liver, local ZB on intestine, pancreas, kidneys, feet, spine with massage for 5 minutes each, local KL on pancreas 5x5 minutes, heels 20 minutes; next 7 days: local KL on pancreas 5x5 minutes, heels 20 minutes, local RC - intestine for 5 minutes, pancreas, kidneys, liver, bladder for 10 minutes, local ZB on intestine, pancreas, kidneys, liver, bladder, spine with massage for 5 minutes, sitz bath (pair) 30 minutes + local KL on bladder 15 minutes; next 6 days: local KL on pancreas 5x5 minutes, heels 20 minutes, local GI - intestine, pancreas, kidneys, liver for 10 minutes, local ZC on intestine, pancreas, kidneys, liver for 5 minutes, bladder 10 minutes, spine with massage for 5 minutes, pair GI+KL on bladder 30 minutes; last 7 days AV + ZC general 10-15-20 minutes, general KL for 10 minutes. Result : General condition improved, felt invigorated, sleep normalized, perineal itching, mouth bitterness, and dryness no longer bother, urination frequency reduced, on the 9th day of therapy, edema and infiltration on the right foot's little toe disappeared, scab fell off on the 10th day. On day 11, blood sugar 9 mmol/L, no sugar in urine, on day 21 of therapy, blood sugar 6.8 mmol/L, on day 24, liver size reduced to +2 – 2.5 cm, coagulogram data normalized, REG - satisfactory blood filling of leg arteries, venous tone normal, CBC normal. Stopped taking antidiabetic medication after treatment.

Patient, age 39, sought medical help due to back pain caused by spinal deformity. From the medical history: she has repeatedly consulted manual therapists and received physiotherapeutic treatment but did not experience significant improvement. Upon examination, the patient has a pronounced thoracic kyphosis and lumbar lordosis. She was prescribed a course of treatment with an infrared emitter GI and KL daily for 30-45 minutes, along with a spine massage using the ZB emitter for 5 minutes. As a result of the therapy, after 10 days, the patient's back pain significantly decreased, and the manifestations of kyphosis and lordosis almost disappeared.

Patient, age 46. During the course of therapy using the ceramic emitter P2M combined with the blood normalizer Kr-1 (developed by the Research Center "RRH"), the following changes occurred: On the first day of irradiation totaling 30 minutes — 5 minutes each in the axillary lymph node area, on the right side of the chest, and at the primary site of damage. By the next day, at the time of the second session, the volume of the affected axillary lymph nodes had decreased by 2/3 from their initial size, the painful lumps palpable the previous day on the right side of the chest had completely resolved, and the primary site of damage — carcinoma — became significantly softer and reduced in size. Irradiation was carried out for three consecutive days for 30 minutes each, resulting in the complete resolution of the axillary lymph nodes and the primary tumor volume reduced by half. Currently, there is a break in treatment.

Patient S.O., a 5-year-old boy. Five congenital heart defects, including VSD and ASD. Moderate physical activity leads to peripheral and central cyanosis. Surgical intervention was proposed, even with the prospect of temporary and limited improvement, but the parents refused. Currently, complaints include chronic cough, mostly accompanied by vomiting. Vomit attacks occur no less than 10 times a day. Whenever the child goes out, parents always carry a plastic bag because he might cough and vomit, especially after eating. The family approached the clinic to have the boy undergo a course of resonant IR therapy. Significant improvement was not expected due to structural defects, but the parents decided to try. The treatment mainly involved the use of RV, RC, GI, and ZB emitters on the chest and heart area.

Patient, age 43. Medical history: Four months before the start of therapy, diagnosed with a left ovarian cyst measuring 5 x 5 cm. Surgery was planned but postponed by the patient. She came to the Infra Life clinic where mainly RC and ZB emitters were used on the ovary. The treatment duration was 14 sessions, almost daily. Immediately after completing the 14 sessions, the patient visited the same gynecologist, and a follow-up ultrasound was performed: the cyst was not detected.

Patient, age 42. Complaints: Ovarian cyst and tumor Psoriasis Infertility The primary reason for the consultation is the ovarian cyst and psoriasis. History: Married for 12 years but never pregnant. Extensive examinations have been performed, including 7 general anesthesias for procedures like laparoscopy and GIFT. She refused further examination and sought alternative treatment for the ovarian cyst. Additionally, the patient has psoriasis on the scalp, trunk, and limbs, especially in the flexural areas, which appeared within 10 days. An ovarian ultrasound was performed by a gynecologist before the start of therapy. The ovarian diameter was 3.5 cm, however, in addition to the cyst, the gynecologist found a solid structure inside the ovary, thus diagnosing an ovarian tumor. As the nature of the tumor (benign or malignant) was unknown, the patient was advised to undergo urgent cytological examination of the tissue. She refused and opted for a course of infrared therapy. Treatment Results : After 10 days of therapy, the same gynecologist repeated the ultrasound, and the largest diameter of the tumor was 3.1 cm. Attempts were made to measure the largest possible diameter, but only this measurement was obtained. Thus, the cyst size reduced by 3 mm in 10 days. Unfortunately, the patient could not continue treatment due to work obligations. Psoriasis lesions became less pronounced and flatter. Improvement was noticed immediately after the second day of therapy, with complete skin clearance achieved after 10 days as expected. No side effects. Comments: Since the patient was unable to continue treatment, further observation by a gynecologist and adherence to the treatment plan by the attending physician are recommended. The full course of therapy was not completed, but there was a reduction in the size of the ovarian tumor.

Patient P.N., a 7-year-old girl. Complaints of abdominal pain, colic, and diarrhea. This condition lasted for an hour, and the girl was crying from pain. The RV emitter was used for 2 minutes, followed by the GI emitter for 10 minutes. Result : The pain completely subsided, and the diarrhea stopped immediately. No side effects observed. Comments : Abdominal colic and diarrhea, in most cases, arise from viruses or bacteria, which are considered the cause in 90% of such problems. A significant number of patients with these issues have been treated with this method, yielding exclusively good results. Symptomatic relief and cessation of diarrhea occur very quickly after two or three 15-minute sessions each hour. Often, the effect is immediate after the first therapy session.

Patient, age 24, came with complaints of migraine attacks for 12 months. Attacks occur at least 3 times a week, characterized by pulsating headache lasting a day. Provoking factors include rapidly changing weather, such as a hot day followed by a rainy one, and cold air from air conditioning. The IR therapy consisted of 7 sessions. The treatment aimed at normalizing the function of all organs based on EAF indicators. One week after starting the treatment, the patient had only one mild, short attack. An examination a month later showed no recurrence of headaches. No side effects were observed.

Patient, age 24, unmarried. Came with complaints of migraines for 12 months. Pulsating headaches usually last a day. Attacks occur at least 3 times a week. Aggravating factors include rapidly changing weather, like a hot day followed by a rainy one. Additionally, she works in a bank where there's strong air conditioning blowing directly at her. Treatment : 7 sessions, mainly focusing on normalizing the function of all systemic organs based on EAF indicators. Follow-up examination after one week: Only one mild, short attack in the last week. Examination after a month showed that the headache had stopped. Recommended to return for treatment for a few days every 3-6 months. The patient lives far away and cannot attend regular check-ups. No side effects observed.

sections.title: MIGRAINE
paragraphs: Patient, a 45-year-old male. Complaints of severe migraine attacks and high blood pressure. Migraine attacks 1-3 times a week for the last 10 years, hypertension for 5-6 years. Migraine attacks are always sudden, lasting from 2 to 5 hours, and resolve just as abruptly, accompanied by vomiting, trembling, and increased frequency with lack of sleep. The headaches come and go suddenly, during which the patient must lie down, and medication does not relieve the pain. All types of preventive measures have been tried without success. Currently, the patient does not take any medications for migraines. Additionally, he was diagnosed with hypertension a year ago for which he takes antihypertensive medication to maintain blood pressure at 140-150/95-105. At the time of consultation at Infra-life Clinic, he was taking Lecidiphil 8 mg/day (usual dose 2 mg). EAF indicators were 80 at most points. A course of RT with the "INFRA R" method was started — only three sessions were conducted. The main emitters used were RV, GI, KH, and ZB. No side effects were observed. Result: Since the start of treatment, there have been no migraine attacks, even when the patient slept only a few hours a day. Two weeks later, he returned and continued treatment for another 7 days. A month later, he sent a letter stating there had been no migraine attacks. The patient was observed for another 5 months, during which time no migraine attacks occurred, and his blood pressure stabilized at 120-130/70-80.

Patient S., a 35-year-old woman. Complaints of frequent migraine attacks, averaging once every 1-2 months for two years, which have increased in frequency over the last year. Each attack lasts several hours throughout the day, characterized by pulsating pain on one side, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. Partial relief is achieved with mefenamic acid. When an attack starts, the patient cannot continue working and must lie down. A course of IR therapy was conducted using RV, ZB, and GI emitters, for which there was a reaction based on EAF indicators. Therapy was performed daily for a total of 10 sessions. Result : The patient stopped attending as the attacks ceased and did not reappear for 3 months. Recommended to come for check-ups every 3 months and possibly need treatment for a few days if EAF indicators deviate. She returned after 3 months due to a mild attack after a long trip from Malacca. Since then, migraine attacks are very rare and mild. Comments : This method is good for preventing migraine attacks. Most patients experience a curative effect, but one should expect significant relief in terms of less frequent and less intense attacks. This treatment is not applied during an attack since it can only provide partial relief for headache reduction, not better than painkillers. The therapy aims to normalize the body's condition and blood circulation in the spinal and brain areas, which is a slow process requiring 10 to 20 days.

Patient R., male, 45 years old. Complaints of severe migraine attacks and high blood pressure. Migraine attacks occur 1-3 times a week for the past 10 years, hypertension for 5-6 years. Migraine episodes are always sudden, lasting 2-5 hours, and resolve just as suddenly, accompanied by vomiting, trembling, and increased frequency with lack of sleep. The patient must isolate himself in a room and lie down for several hours until the attack abruptly ends. All types of preventive measures have been tried without success. When an attack starts, no medications help, so the patient no longer takes any medication for this. In addition, the patient is taking two types of medications for hypertension. One year before starting resonance therapy, he was hospitalized for a week with blood pressure at 220/130 even during sleep. He was discharged with better blood pressure control, his usual BP being 140-150/95-105. He tried various medications until his diastolic pressure reached 90 mmHg. At the time of consultation at Infra-life Clinic, he was taking Lecidiphil 8 mg/day (usual dose 2 mg). EAF indicators were 80 at most points. A course of resonance IR therapy was started, but only three sessions were conducted due to time constraints. The main emitters used were RV, GI, KH, and ZB. No side effects were observed. Result : Since the start of treatment, there have been no migraine attacks, even when the patient slept only a few hours. On his return journey, he drove for 9 hours straight without a stop, but there was no attack, contrary to his expectations. Two weeks later, he returned and continued treatment for another 7 days. After a month, he sent a letter stating that there had been no attacks. It has been 5 months since the first session, and he has still not had a single attack, with blood pressure maintained at 120-130/70-80.

Patient, 41 years old. Complaints: Suffering from insufficient erection and absence of ejaculation for 2 years. Medical history: Diagnosed with type II diabetes, taking Glibenclimide 5 mg. Married for 7 years, no children. He notes an erection only once every two weeks, sufficient to start sexual intercourse but not to continue, and in most cases, there's no ejaculation or orgasm. He also reports numbness in his legs (up to mid-calf), general weakness, and malaise. Treatment : The patient was treated for 7 days. After the 4th session, sexual intercourse became possible every other day, with normal erection and ejaculation. He continued treatment twice and then once a month for 3 months. As a result of the therapy, blood sugar levels decreased from 8-11 mmol/L to normal. After the treatment ended, the patient remained under observation. He noticed a decrease in erection 8 months after stopping treatment, but the numbness in his feet did not return, and blood sugar levels remained within normal limits. After a repeat course of therapy, he again reported improved potency. No side effects or symptoms were observed.

Patient H., female, 30 years old, married, with a 1.5-year-old child, came with complaints of abdominal swelling and edema of both legs from the ankles down for 6 months. Diagnosed with idiopathic nephrotic syndrome HSA, JB. Skin on the legs is glossy, edema significant, making wearing shoes difficult. Additionally, there's ascites. At the start of therapy, she was taking prednisolone 15 mg daily, T. Lasix 20 mg, T. Slow K. Four months before these events, she had herpes zoster complicating the right chest, leaving a scar after healing. However, the prednisolone dose cannot be reduced due to worsening symptoms and proteinuria. Protein in urine was three plus (+++), serum albumin 16 mg/dl. These levels are typical for most of her tests. She underwent a month of resonance therapy daily. Result : Leg edema noticeably decreased, returning the legs to normal size. Protein in urine reduced to ++, but serum albumin remained between 13-16 mg/dl. The supervising therapist reduced the daily prednisolone dose to 10 mg. Serum protein increased to +++, but serum albumin stayed the same. Waist circumference reduced by 3 cm. Body weight decreased from 45 to 40 kg, possibly due to tissue fluid loss (reduced edema). An interesting observation was that the legs returned to normal size after 20 days of treatment, allowing for a two-thirds reduction in prednisolone (to 5 mg daily), discontinuation of Lasix and Slow K. After 30 days of therapy, she was advised to come weekly. The clinical picture remained unchanged, with no further improvement in biochemical tests. Therefore, treatment was stopped. A longer course was not feasible as the patient came from far away and had to take a month off work. Side Effect : After the fifth session, pinpoint hemorrhages and knee pain were noted on one leg. These symptoms resolved within a week of continuing treatment. Comments : Notably, the ZB emitter clearly affected the reduction of excess fluid in the leg vessels, while serum protein levels remained unchanged. However, the prednisolone dose was reduced by two-thirds compared to the initial dose. In this case, there was significant symptomatic improvement.

In the patient tested by Folle, numbers below normal were found at the control point of the renal cortex. The patient does not complain of kidney pain, and the urine test is normal. Emitters GI, AF, and RV do not test at the renal cortex point, indicating no pathological process in this organ. The effectiveness of the ZB emitter on the arterial point was noted, where applying it improved the readings at the renal cortex points.

Patient, age 39. An infiltrative growth in the breast tissue was palpable. Six daily irradiations of 12 minutes each were conducted, resulting in significant softening of the tumor tissue, with complete dissolution of cancer-affected tissue observed in some areas.

Patient, male, 34 years old. Complaints of elevated uric acid levels despite adhering to a diet, recurring pain in the metatarsophalangeal joints once a month for 2 years. At the time of admission to Infra Life Clinic, he had been suffering from continuous joint pain for 2 months. Uric acid - 7-8 mg/dl. For 2 months, he has been receiving NSAIDs injections 4 times a day and orally. On examination, joints are hot, painful, and swollen. Pain is pulsating, interfering with sleep and daily work, walking is difficult. A course of RT was conducted using the GI emitter. Result : After 3 days of treatment, the pain significantly decreased, and within a week, the inflammatory process in the joints completely resolved, and pain disappeared. Four months later, at the time of this report, the patient is still in remission.

Patient admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of acute exacerbation of chronic prostatitis, complaining of lower abdominal pain and dysuria symptoms. Treatment: Use of the "CT" setup for 10 minutes and ZB(s) on the bladder area for 10 minutes (simultaneously). Treatment continued for 10 days. The result was a complete remission of the condition.

Patient, 42 years old, admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of obesity. With a height of 164 cm, his weight was 103 kg. He received a general course of IR therapy for 1 month, after which weight loss was observed. No further treatment courses were conducted. More than two years have passed since the treatment, and the patient's current weight is 72 kg (not adhering to a diet).

Patient, 11 years old, admitted to the clinic with a diagnosis of acute respiratory viral infection. Ill for two weeks with high fever, runny nose, tearing, and severe headache. Treated with antibiotics and painkillers without improvement. On examination: pharynx hyperemic, tonsil arches swollen, conjunctiva hyperemic, mucous discharge from the nose. EAF diagnostics showed high readings (above 78) on almost all meridians. Treatment included RC(b) using a floating scheme for 7 days, RC(s) on the head and spinal cord area for 3 days, GI(b) from 15 to 30 minutes according to the scheme + KL(b) for 15 minutes for 7 days. As a result of the therapy, headaches and fever normalized after the first session. Nasal discharge stopped on the third day.

Patient admitted to the clinic with signs of acute cystitis. After one session, which included local exposure to the bladder through the anterior abdominal wall and perineum using the "CT" setup, all symptoms of acute cystitis were alleviated within 30 minutes - frequent, painful urination, abdominal pain, and voiding in small amounts.

Patient, 38 years old. Poisoning occurred after ingesting a solution composed of several chemicals. She mixed Polyethylene glycol, chlorhexidine, Dettol, Ethanol, erythromycin ointment, and alcohol, then drank the mixture. Three hours later, she was admitted, still conscious. Mild hand tremors, hyperkinesis, complaints of epigastric pain, and she repeatedly said, "Doctor, help." Gastric lavage was performed, but the pain did not decrease. All EAF points were around 100 and unresponsive to most emitters, except KH on the pituitary and RC on the liver and general RC. After 5 minutes of exposure with the KH emitter on the head and general RC, readings dropped only to 70, but the patient felt better, and the tremors almost ceased. The EAF device also showed reduced readings on the liver and all meridians under RC. Three sessions were conducted in one day. Epigastric pain did not immediately subside with any emitter, but within 2 days, the patient fully recovered and was discharged. Comments: In this case, a symptomatic response of the body was observed. The exact effect on the expulsion of chemicals is not established due to the lack of tracking means. Further study is required.

sections.title: PARACETAMOL POISONING
paragraphs: Patient S., female, 31 years old. Family issues led to divorce, causing the patient to take 50 paracetamol tablets at once. Three days later, she sought help, complaining of excessive drowsiness and loss of appetite. No vomiting occurred after taking the tablets. Her statement was questioned by several doctors, but she insisted she counted the tablets. Her ex-husband, still caring for her, was informed that she would likely need hemodialysis, but not at home. Medical examination: Drowsiness, lethargy, jaundice. Due to dehydration, she received intravenous fluids. She was offered to try IR therapy, with the understanding that if unsuccessful, she would need daily hemodialysis based on further assessment, to which she agreed. A 5-day treatment course was conducted, mainly using the RC emitter on the liver (a reaction to this emitter was noted with EAF). The results were very interesting; jaundice did not progress, and all liver enzymes normalized. Blood biochemical markers are as follows: Day Before treatment Day 1 Day 2 Day 3 Day 7 Date 13/9/98 14/9/98 15/9/98 23/9/98 Total bilirubin 1.8 1.4 1.1 1.0 1.0 Direct bilirubin 1.5 0.9 0.4 0.6 0.5 Indirect bilirubin 0.3 0.5 0.7 0.4 0.5 Total protein 71 56 66 63 72 Albumin 34 27 31 30 37 Globulin 37 29 35 33 35 A/g ratio 0.9 0.9 0.9 1.0 1.1 Alp 55 51 51 64 52 AСT 1884 1412 1000 782 15 ALT 2252 1028 561 252 27 The patient was discharged from the hospital after 4 days, and a test a week later showed that liver enzymes were normal. She survived without hemodialysis, and jaundice did not progress. No side effects were observed. Comments: The treatment yielded excellent results. It is recommended to study more cases of poisoning accompanied by liver damage in the future.
