The patient, born in 1971, visited the clinic due to the absence of pregnancy, as well as complaints of pain in the right inguinal area, increased pain during sexual intercourse, and a prolonged menstrual cycle. From the history : she has been sexually active for 3 years without contraception, no pregnancy occurred, menstruation is delayed by 2-3 weeks. On examination : The cervix appeared clean in the speculum; per vaginum, the uterus is of normal size, painless, firm, and mobile. The left adnexa are unremarkable, but those on the right are dense and painful. Discharge is moderate and mucous. Laboratory and instrumental examination showed: Hemoglobin (Hb) - 90 g/L; Leukocytes (L) - 6.0; Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) - 3 mm/h. Ultrasound showed the uterus measuring 60x45x57 mm, shifted to the right, with a homogeneous structure. The right ovary is 36x25 mm with microcystic changes, the left ovary not visualized. The patient received treatment with anti-inflammatory and antibacterial devices, as well as devices normalizing blood circulation and dissolving pathological connective tissue - both general and local (on the ovaries) procedures. Daily procedures were conducted to stimulate immunity and regulate the vegetative nervous system. By the 7th day of treatment, the pain disappeared; after the 15th session, the right adnexa were painless, no palpable strands, and the discharge was serous, scant. After a month of therapy, lab results showed: Hb - 110 g/L; L - 5.0 g/L; ESR - 5 mm/h. The ultrasound of the uterus indicated a 4-week pregnancy. The right ovary measured 26x28 mm, the left 30x26 mm.

A patient, born in 1984, came to the clinic complaining of no menstruation for 7 months, weakness, dizziness, and decreased work capacity. Diagnosis - amenorrhea. In her history : For 5 months, she adhered to a strict diet excluding protein (eating only tomatoes and apples) to lose weight, losing 12 kg during this period. A month after starting the diet, her next menstruation did not occur. She consulted a gynecologist where no pathology in the genital organs was found. Measurement of basal temperature over 3 months showed a monophasic cycle. She received progesterone treatment to stimulate menstruation, which was ineffective. Upon admission, she had pallor of the skin, and unsatisfactory subcutaneous fat development (weighing 50 kg at 170 cm tall). The therapy was aimed at normalizing the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, stimulating organs responsible for adaptive mechanisms. During treatment with narrow-spectrum devices, she measured basal temperature. On the 6th day of treatment, an increase in basal temperature to 37°C was noted, indicating normalization of the ovarian cycle. Menstruation began on the 12th day of therapy. The patient was observed for 3 months during which time her menstruations were regular, moderate, painless, with a cycle of 28-30 days.

A 17-year-old male patient, in 1996, was involved in a car accident and suffered multiple injuries (fracture of the ischial bone, fractures of the tibia, and two fractures of the femur). He spent a long time in the trauma unit where he underwent two surgeries for the fractures. Post-operatively, he noted an inability to urinate independently, requiring catheterization. He was discharged with recommendations for further surgical treatment in urology departments, where urethral reconstruction was recommended, or, if surgery was refused, lifelong weekly urethral dilation. In February 1997, he sought our help, refusing surgical treatment. An urethrocystography performed on 05.02.1997 showed a large bend in the prostatic part of the urethra and a fracture of the ischial bone in two places, with displacement in the lower part. He was troubled by difficult urination with a weak, bifurcated stream. He underwent urethral dilation every 5 days. After the 1st session of ZB + KL (local, 10 minutes), the patient felt increased warmth during urination. After the 3rd session, the urine stream became stronger, the color of the urine changed, and there was a presence of blood in the stream. Dilation was performed every 7 days. After the 6th session of ZB, dilation was noted to be easier. Before treatment, there was a step-like obstruction (at least 3-4 steps), now only one step remained. Urgency to urinate appeared, with a full urine stream. After the 9th-10th session of ZB, the dilator passed freely, with slight resistance at the end. Following this, he was sent for a control urethrocystogram, which showed a significant smoothing of the "bend" at the transition from the prostatic to the membranous urethra. Dilation was performed every 18 days. Another course of ZB - 10 sessions, KL - 6 sessions, and KB - 6 sessions on the pelvic bones in the fracture area for 1-2 minutes each was completed, after which dilation was discontinued. The urine stream became full, and urination was free. The control x-ray on 30.04.1997 showed that the patient had fully recovered due to infrared therapy.

A 24-year-old female patient. Initially, in the affected area: In the area of the right zygomatic arch, four hard, bone-like growths adhered to the bone were palpable, of various sizes. During the course of treatment with an emitter based on ceramic material P2M (10W), there was a rapid reduction in all four tumors; they lost their connection with the underlying bone tissue, organized into a fibrous capsule, became mobile, and very soft. Currently, the patient is preparing for surgical removal of the remaining pathologically altered tissue. A total of 10 daily treatments for 20 minutes each were applied.

Patient A.M., a 54-year-old woman. The patient has elevated cholesterol levels with a total cholesterol to HDL-cholesterol ratio of 6.1. Cholesterol levels have remained high for many years, with high levels of triglycerides and LDL-cholesterol as well. A course of resonant infrared therapy was conducted, primarily using GI and ZB emitters on the gallbladder. Results : After one week of treatment, there was an increase in HDL-cholesterol and normalization of triglyceride and LDL-cholesterol levels. The ratio of total cholesterol to HDL-cholesterol decreased to 4.1 within a week, although it had remained high for years despite avoiding high-cholesterol foods. No side effects were observed. Comments : With this treatment method, cholesterol levels are easily normalized; it's best to conduct treatment immediately after eating.

A patient, born in 1985, was admitted to the clinic with complaints of constant bleeding from the genital tract for 2 months, dizziness, weakness, and decreased work capacity. Diagnosis - juvenile uterine bleeding. From the history : For 9 months, menstrual cycle disturbances in the form of prolonged bleeding have been noted. The onset of the disease is not associated with any specific cause. She has repeatedly received hemostatic and uterotonic treatments, synthetic progestins for 3 months without effect. Upon admission : The skin was pale, Hb - 80 g/L, anisopoikilocytosis present, pelvic ultrasound showed no signs of echopathology. Using electroacupuncture diagnostics according to R. Voll, there was a significant decrease in readings on all meridians. Treatment with narrow-spectrum infrared emitters was aimed at normalizing the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian system, stimulating organs responsible for adaptive mechanisms, as well as immunostimulatory and anti-inflammatory therapy. Results : Bleeding stopped on the 5th day of treatment, by the 12th day, Hb was at 112 g/L. Subsequent observation for 2 months revealed no recurrence of bleeding.

A 55-year-old patient. Suffering from asthma for 2 years, she experiences daily morning asthma attacks accompanied by stridor and shortness of breath. She constantly requires medication. The use of an inhaler does not relieve the attacks. Treatment : The patient underwent a 7-day course of resonant therapy, mainly using GI and ZB emitters on the gallbladder and adrenal glands. Results : After 3 days of treatment, medication use was completely stopped, and there were no more attacks. She returned to her hometown. After the treatment course, there were no asthma attacks, and medication use was discontinued. Six weeks later, she came for a follow-up visit, during which time there had been no asthma attacks. Five months later, she traveled to Mecca, and upon returning, she experienced mild asthma attacks for two days, after which she returned to the Infra Life clinic. After 2 days, she felt well, with no asthma attacks noted. No side effects were observed.

A patient, born in 1982, diagnosed with psoriasis - widespread form, progressive course, mixed type. Upon admission, complaints were of rashes all over the body with severe itching, irritability, sleep and appetite disturbances. From the history: Alongside the diagnosis of adenoid vegetations of the second degree at the age of 4, the boy was diagnosed with pseudo-psoriasis. After adenoidectomy, the pseudo-psoriasis symptoms disappeared. Since 1992, nasal congestion became a concern again, diagnosed with a deviated nasal septum. In 1993, spots with scaling appeared on the scalp. The patient was treated at the skin dispensary of the railway medical unit for 2 years, after which complete remission was noted. In 1996, rashes in the form of plaques appeared on the scalp and body. From October 6, 1996, the patient was treated with the "Salut" device (a development by Dr. Fischer AO in Vaduz: an apparatus producing a pulsating current that creates a magnetic field in the system). During the treatment (5th-6th session), the number and size of plaques increased, and the condition worsened until November 1996. Submucosal resection of the nasal septum was performed amidst the psoriasis exacerbation in November 1996. The patient repeatedly received treatment in Moscow at the Central Clinical Hospital, took hormones and cytostatics, and tried unconventional methods from folk healers. No improvement was noted; the condition progressed. On examination, plaques of congestive red color, covered with flat silvery scales and merging, are clearly visible on the skin of the upper part of the head, face, torso, arms, and legs. Rashes cover more than 80% of the skin surface. The nail plates are like thimbles (with minute pitting). For 3 months, the patient received therapy with resonant infrared emitters GI and KL. After the 10th session, stabilization of the condition was noted, and itching completely ceased. After 1.5 months, the face, neck, and back were almost clear of elements. By the end of treatment, all skin was completely free from pathological elements. The patient has been observed for 3 years by our clinic's doctors, and no recurrence of the disease has been noted.

A 36-year-old female patient. Has been suffering from psoriasis for 2 years. Complaints include psoriasis lesions on the skin all over the body; joint pain when moving, with movement range reduced by 30% (sometimes due to sharp limitations in knee joint mobility, the patient has to urinate standing up). For the past year, she has also experienced severe, dull pain in the right scapula area. On examination, the skin condition is widespread. Psoriasis plaques, which are pinkish-red and covered with silvery scales, merge and cover the entire back, hips, and calves. On the arms, the lesions are more prominent on the extensor surfaces. On the scalp, there are multiple scaly papules. The knee joints are erythematous and swollen. Consulted by an orthopedic surgeon who believes these pains are of psoriatic nature. The patient received 34 sessions of "INFRA R" resonant therapy (RT). Results : Skin lesions diminished daily. After 25 sessions, the skin was completely clear except for a few spots on the back and head. Joint pain decreased, movement range increased to 60%, but movements are still limited (cannot fully squat). After 30 sessions, over a period of 2 weeks, the patient came for treatment twice a week. Consequently, the skin on the arms and legs cleared almost completely except for scar areas, with only a few new lesions appearing on the head. Pain in the scapula decreased by half. After a day's rest from treatment, further reduction in knee joint pain was noted. Home treatment with several emitters was recommended to maintain the therapeutic effect, but the patient declined. Remission lasted for 8 months. The relapse was characterized by less extensive skin lesions and reduced joint pain intensity. Side Effects : Severe joint pains and cold symptoms for 5 days, leading to confinement to a wheelchair for 4 days due to inability to walk; however, after this, she was able to walk normally, and even better than before starting treatment. Comments : In this case, near-complete remission was achieved. During the therapy course, there was a side effect of arthralgia. Therefore, it is suggested to determine the optimal exposure duration or to start treatment with lower exposure and increase it as tolerated.

A 65-year-old male patient. Presented with complaints of back pain at the level of the scapula and pain in the left thigh. The pain is dull, worsening over the last two months. During this time, he has also experienced progressive difficulties with urination and defecation due to the lack of urge and ability to strain. Every 4-5 days, he is forced to take laxatives or perform an enema. The patient also cannot feel or control urination, requiring a catheter with 4-hour intervals for urination. All symptoms have been gradually worsening over two months. He cannot walk but can stand with support. Most pain-relieving medications do not provide complete relief. Blood biochemistry and hematological profile - normal. Chest X-ray : One large lesion extends beyond the left cardiac shadow, another is located in the left lateral middle lobe of the lung, presumably with metastases. Ultrasound : No focal lesions in the liver, kidneys normal, prostate enlarged. CT scan of the head showed multiple large lesions in the brain's meninges. MRI of the spinal cord : Altered bone marrow signal in the cervical, thoracic, lumbar, and sacral regions at multiple levels. There is a pathological compression fracture at the T3 vertebra, associated with a paravertebral mass extending from T1 to T5 and an epidural mass from T2 to T4, causing spinal compression. At the S2 level, another large tumor is located in the middle and left side, narrowing the sacral spinal canal and likely affecting the nerve endings of the left sacral plexus. These findings are primarily due to metastatic involvement. Based on all symptoms, a diagnosis of lung cancer with metastases to the lungs, thoracic spine, sacrum, and brain meninges was made. The patient was recommended radiotherapy, but he sought alternatives and, upon hearing about treatment with special IR radiation according to the Rahimov method, decided to try it. In his case, radiotherapy had not yet been performed. After being informed that the so-called RC emitter has the effect of recombination of radicals with high activation energy and, theoretically, could reduce or stop growth, with or without symptomatic relief, he wished to try the treatment. He was treated for 14 days, mainly using RC, GI, and ZB with brief exposure. Results : The results were astonishing, with significant symptomatic relief. After 3 days, there was complete relief from sacral spine pain. The primary issue was pain in the left thigh, which diminished after 10 days and did not return. Bowel movements were restored after 7 days (once every two days) and then daily after a few more days. Urination also became independent, and the catheter was removed. He can walk short distances. Discharged from the hospital, recommended to continue treatment at home with 4 types of emitters (RC, GI, ZB, KL). Ten days later, the patient could walk with a cane and looked very happy. After another 2 weeks (3.5 weeks post-discharge), he arrived without a cane. Before treatment, he was prescribed a wheelchair. All symptomatic improvements were maintained for one month. He stopped treatment when he felt the emitter was no longer effective. A week later, his leg was paralyzed again, and sacral spine pain returned. He came for treatment and received RV emitter therapy. After one session, the pain significantly decreased and stayed at that level. Comments : Theoretically, treatment might halt cancer growth. In some patients, symptomatic relief is expected when the body's immune system restores normal metabolic processes in the lesion site, especially after the ZB emitter, which aids in tumor resorption to a certain extent and improves blood circulation. The better the clinical condition and organ function, the more effective results we can expect because treatment, in these cases, can be conducted without interference. In patients who have not undergone radio- or chemotherapy, we expect better clinical outcomes. This therapy method can be used for symptomatic treatment of cancer patients.

A 53-year-old male patient. Diagnosis: Bladder cancer and TURP were established one year before starting resonant therapy (RT) using IR. Nine months before RT, intravenous urography (IVU) revealed bilateral hydronephrosis, but the patient refused surgery. Symptoms include urinary incontinence (constant dripping), urethral blockage during urination due to TURP fibrotic complications, causing pain at the base of the urethra when attempting to urinate, requiring constant urethral massage. Sometimes, there's a dull pain in the suprapubic area, lasting from a few hours to a whole day for several months. Ultrasound before RT showed bilateral hydronephrosis and thickening of the bladder's posterior wall. RT was conducted daily for 3 weeks. Mainly RC and ZB emitters were used on the bladder. Ultrasound was repeated after 14 days - no hydronephrosis, wall thickening remains unchanged. Urinary incontinence in the form of dripping gradually ceased, starting from the 10th day and almost completely disappeared after 20 therapy sessions over 2 months. Pain during urination due to urethral blockage also reduced, and by his estimation, relief was about 60% (more than 50%) after the 20th session of treatment. Absolutely no side symptoms or signs. He feels well and did not continue treatment after 20 sessions due to the long distance (60 km), as he uses public transport and faces financial difficulties to reach the clinic. Conclusion : RT provided symptomatic relief for the aforementioned patient with bladder cancer.

A 44-year-old male patient with pancreatic cancer. General condition is critically severe, asthenic, consciousness is slowed. Skin is pale, dry, cool to the touch, with reduced turgor. Body temperature is 35.6°C. The abdomen is sharply painful upon palpation, the liver is not palpable. On EAF testing: on the BAT of the SPED meridian 12. With the application of the RC emitter, the reading on the BAT of the SPED meridian rose from 12 to 24, and the needle started to fall after 10 seconds, but exposure should continue until the needle drops (according to the formula above) to 18 ((24-12)/2+12). This improves the functional activity of the organ or its part and extends exposure time.

sections.title: RHEUMATISM, RHEUMATIC CARDITIS, MITRAL-AORTIC DEFECT, RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS
paragraphs: A female patient, born in 1966, admitted in severe condition with a diagnosis - Rheumatism, activity I-II, recurrent rheumatic carditis, mitral-aortic defect, rheumatoid arthritis. Complaints include extreme weakness, shortness of breath, malaise, tachycardia attacks only relieved by cardiac glycosides, severe restriction of mobility in all joints (hip, knee, ankle, shoulder, elbow, and wrist). The patient arrived with family members as she could not care for herself. BP 180/120, later 160/100. In her medical history, she has been repeatedly treated in hospital for 4-5 years, receiving hormonal therapy (5 tablets of prednisolone daily) for 3 years. Treatment was conducted with GI(s) and ZB(s) emitters on the intestines, RC(s) on the liver and spleen area, then GI(s) and ZB(s) on the liver area, followed by both sides of the adrenal glands, RC(s) and ZB(s) on all joints for 10-15 minutes. The first treatment course lasted 1 month, followed by a 2-week break. As a result, swelling in all joints disappeared, the patient could dress and move independently, BP stabilized around 130/80, tachycardia attacks sharply decreased, almost gone. After the two-week break, she returned for further treatment, which followed the same scheme but focused mainly on the liver and adrenal glands. Thanks to the therapy, she is active, moves freely, and her condition is satisfactory. Currently, she does not require hormonal medications.

A patient, born in 1948, came to the clinic with complaints of pain and swelling in the knee and ankle joints, stiffness throughout the day, chest pain, and cough. Diagnosis - Rheumatoid arthritis, slowly progressing course, activity stage III, seronegative. Ill since 1986. Recently, pain has intensified, especially in the spine, knees, and ankles, with swelling, difficulty bending, and walking. BP - 150/90 mmHg. In the lungs, there are isolated dry rales. The spine is non-tender on palpation. Ritchie Index 34 points; VAS - 10; ESR - 130 mm/h. EAF diagnostics : Readings on all meridians are below normal (24-48), but on the liver and joint meridians, readings are above normal (72-88). On the kidney meridian at the bladder point, values were significantly higher than normal (18-28-32). 18 treatment sessions were conducted. Stiffness has somewhat decreased, although it persisted throughout the day. Movement in the shoulder, wrist, knee, and ankle joints was significantly eased. Pain in other joints has been reduced. The cough is no longer a concern. Upon examination - the Ritchie Index after treatment scored 10 points, VAS - 4. Vesicular breath sounds in the lungs. Heart sounds are slightly muffled. Blood pressure - 130/85; ESR - 135 mm/h.

A patient arrived at the clinic with a cut wound on the middle third of the left forearm. Forty minutes before admission, he fell onto a sharp metal object. On admission, he complained of pain at the wound site, fever, and bleeding. Upon examination: there is a cut wound with clean edges, measuring 10x5 cm on the back of the middle third of the left forearm. There is venous bleeding from the wound, with the wound bed composed of damaged muscles. Movement of the limb is restricted. The patient was treated with the GI(s) emitter on the wound and intestines for 10-15 minutes twice a day, and KL(s) on the pancreas and hypothalamus for 5 minutes twice a day. Results : By the 5th day, the wound healed by primary intention.

A patient, born in 1966, was admitted in a severe condition complaining of extreme weakness, shortness of breath, malaise, tachycardia attacks relieved only by cardiac glycosides, severe restriction of mobility in all joints (hip, knee, ankle, shoulder, elbow, and wrist), with BP 180/120 then 160/100. She first became ill 5 years ago, has been repeatedly treated in hospital, and has received hormone therapy (25 mg prednisolone 3 times a day) for 3 years. Diagnosis: Rheumatism, activity I-II, recurrent rheumatic carditis, mitral-aortic defect, rheumatoid arthritis. Treatment was conducted using the "INFRA R" RT method, with emitters providing anti-inflammatory effects and normalizing microcirculation. Simultaneously, procedures were carried out with the use of UICI aimed at normalizing lipid metabolism and gut microflora. The patient underwent 2 treatment courses with a 2-week break. The first course lasted one month. The results of the first course included: Elimination of swelling in all joints Normalization of gastrointestinal function The patient could dress and move independently BP stabilized at 130/80 Tachycardia attacks sharply decreased, almost disappearing. After a two-week break, the patient returned for continued treatment, following the same scheme but with an emphasis on normalizing lipid metabolism and stimulating glucocorticoid synthesis. Thanks to the treatment, the patient was taken off hormone therapy, became active, and could move freely.

A 22-year-old patient with a history of two spontaneous late miscarriages with hepatosplenomegaly and anasarca. In both cases, the pregnancy termination occurred at 6-7 months. Examination revealed antibodies to cytomegalovirus. Ultrasound of the uterus and ovaries showed signs of chronic endometritis. Upon admission, she complained of severe lower abdominal pain, bloody vaginal discharge, and frequent headaches. The woman received 12 sessions using both general and local emitters such as RV+AF+ZC+KL, and treatment through the perineum with the "CT" setup. The uterus was treated simultaneously through the anterior abdominal wall and the perineum. After 6 sessions, vaginal discharge and lower abdominal pain completely ceased. After 12 sessions, the blood test for cytomegalovirus antibodies was negative. Ultrasound showed the uterus to be of normal shape, structure, and size without echopathology.

A 51-year-old patient had no particular complaints but wished to undergo a treatment course for preventive purposes. After EAF testing, most indicators were above normal, around 60-75. Treatment was mainly conducted with RV, KL, GI, and ZB emitters. The course was not regular, totaling 10 sessions over a month. The patient was almost completely gray. One month after the start of treatment, the patient noticed all hair had turned dark. All short or newly growing hair was also black. No side effects were observed.

Patient Z.M., 36 years old, suffers from pain in many joints, especially in the knees and small joints of the hands. For 4 years, morning stiffness in the joints has been troubling her, with an absolute inability to straighten her knees. Examination by an orthopedic surgeon showed no abnormalities in the blood. The diagnosis of seronegative arthritis was made. A course of RT was conducted, mainly using GI and ZB emitters for a month. Results : No joint pain at night, daytime pain significantly reduced, no morning stiffness. By her own estimation, pain relief was up to 90% compared to before treatment. Two months after treatment cessation, the clinical condition remained at the same level. Comments : This therapy method can provide symptomatic relief for seronegative arthritis. Similar results were observed in two other patients. However, a relapse can occur at any time, so long-term preventive use of GI and ZB emitters is recommended.

Patient R.M., 50 years old, has been suffering from joint pain for 2 years. The main affected joint is the right shoulder, which became "frozen" due to movement restriction. A course of RT using the "INFRA R" method was conducted, mainly using GI and ZB emitters daily for 3 weeks. Results : Complete relief from pain, with the condition maintained for 8 months at the time of this record. No side effects were observed. Note : Eight months later, the patient returned due to pain in the right sacroiliac area that had appeared over the past week. The pain resolved within a week.

Patient Z.M., a 36-year-old woman, suffers from pain in many joints, especially in the knees and small joints of the hands. Morning stiffness in the joints, with an absolute inability to straighten the knees, has persisted for 4 years. Sometimes she cannot walk, and the pain disturbs her sleep. Examination by an orthopedic surgeon showed no blood abnormalities. The diagnosis of seronegative arthritis was made. A course of resonant IR therapy was conducted, mainly using GI and ZB emitters for a month. Results: Pain significantly reduced, no morning stiffness, no joint pain at night. By her own estimation, pain relief was up to 90% compared to before treatment. Two months after treatment cessation, the clinical condition remained at the same level. Comments : This therapy method can provide symptomatic relief for seronegative arthritis. Similar results were observed in two other patients. However, a relapse can occur at any time, so long-term preventive use of GI and ZB emitters is recommended.

A 54-year-old woman came to the clinic with complaints of severe back pain, which prevented her from walking. She has been ill for many years, with the pain intensifying and becoming constant over the last 2 years. Objectively, the patient is overweight; palpation revealed tenderness paraspinally in the sacral area. X-rays showed displacement of the L5-S1 vertebrae. The patient received treatment with IR emitters on the back area GI(s) for 10 minutes focused on the spine, particularly in the lumbar region, followed by spinal massage twice a day with simultaneous application of the ZB(s) emitter. As a result of the therapy, the patient can now walk for up to one hour without back pain.

A 33-year-old patient presented with complaints of pain in the right hand, especially in the fingers, with numbness in the index, middle, and ring fingers, which began two months ago. Symptoms worsen at night after housework. Numbness and pain sometimes disturb sleep. The patient took several medications prescribed by an orthopedic surgeon without improvement. Surgery to relieve the pressure on the wrist was scheduled. She turned to the Infra-Life clinic, and although we were unsure of the therapy's effect, she wanted to try an unconventional approach. EAF readings were high at most points, responding to the RC emitter. A 14-day therapy course was conducted. No improvement was noted in the first 3 days; numbness began to subside after 4 days. By the 10th day, the symptom was completely gone, and the patient was very happy. Side Effects : After the first day of treatment, the patient experienced a severe headache lasting 24 hours, so the second session was postponed by a day. She took paracetamol for pain relief, which provided some relief. Comments : One should try to treat carpal tunnel syndrome before resorting to significant surgical intervention. It seems that the syndrome is a manifestation of chemical process changes in the body.

An 11-year-old patient came with complaints of severe general weakness, constant subfebrile temperature, and joint pain. Examination revealed LE cells, positive C-reactive protein, leukocytes up to 15 in the urine field of view, protein 0.0033%, and an ESR of 30 mm/h. She has been ill for 3 years. Despite treatment, her ESR remained consistently high. On examination, the patient was underweight with a poor appetite. Joints were not deformed. She consistently had a subfebrile temperature of 37.2-37.3°C. Treatment was carried out using an antiviral emitter RV, procedures to restore gut flora (GI) and immunity (KB). After local emitters, general action emitters RC, GI, KB were applied. As a result of the treatment, after 3 weeks, the ESR decreased to 20 mm/h. The temperature rose periodically. The patient's appetite improved, and she started gaining weight.

A 37-year-old patient. The diagnosis was confirmed by a therapist. She has been suffering from chronic recurring joint pains and ulcers for 3 years. She underwent treatment twice in hospital conditions where parenteral nutrition was administered due to an inability to swallow because of severe mouth and throat ulcers. She takes 20 mg of prednisolone daily for 3 years; without it, joint pains intensify, and mouth ulcers worsen. Her weight is 75 kg, with some degree of "moon face." RT using the "INFRA R" method was conducted for 5 days. After the second day of treatment, as a reaction, there was facial swelling with normal serum protein levels, and a slight increase in joint pain. The exposure time of IR emitters was reduced, and the swelling decreased by the 5th day. Over 2 months of treatment, the patient's weight decreased by 15 kg to 60 kg; joint pains and mouth ulcers completely disappeared. The dose of prednisolone was gradually reduced until the drug was completely discontinued. The patient stopped treatment. There were no relapses for 14 months. A relapse manifested with weak recurring joint pains, after which she started taking prednisolone again at 5 mg and returned to our clinic. At the time of this record, the patient is undergoing the third session of a repeat RT course.

sections.title: TEARING, JOINT ACHE, LEG PAIN, VISION LOSS, GENERAL WEAKNESS
paragraphs: A patient born in 1951 was admitted to the clinic complaining of tearing, joint ache, leg pain, vision deterioration, and general weakness. From the history: Considered herself ill for 1.5 years; examined at the Institute of Microbiology and Infectious Diseases where toxoplasmosis (primarily ocular form) - chorioretinitis was diagnosed. On examination: tearing, peripheral lymph nodes enlarged, mainly submandibular and axillary, heart sounds are muffled. Immunological blood test for toxoplasmosis - RFIA result 1:20. For 8 weeks, daily treatment was conducted with both general and local emitters. These included: antiviral (10 min/day), antibacterial and anti-inflammatory (20-90 min/day according to the scheme), immunomodulatory (10 min/day), and circulation-improving (10-15 min/day) emitters. Local emitters were aimed at the brain membranes, lymph nodes, liver, spleen, kidneys, eyes, gallbladder, and intestines. The exposure time for local emitters was adjusted under EAF control. Daily regulation of the vegetative nervous system was also performed. Results : After 3 weeks of treatment, leg and joint pain disappeared; after 8 weeks, tearing ceased, and vision improved. A repeat immunological blood test for toxoplasmosis was negative.

A 62-year-old patient has been suffering from severe back pain for two years after falling from a ladder. Due to the severe pain, she cannot walk, stand, and is forced to remain horizontal. X-rays showed spondylolisthesis at L IV-V. She received treatment for 14 days. Results : Significant improvement; the patient can walk, sit as much as she wants without pain. She can walk without assistance, can bend her knees without pain. Observation period for the patient - 6 months. Pain did not recur. No side effects were observed. Comments : Good treatment effects were observed in two other patients with spondylolisthesis.

An 8-year-old patient presented with progressive involuntary blinking occurring 30-40 times per minute. She has been ill for 6 months. An ophthalmologist's examination found no anomalies. Examined by a therapist, a brain CT scan showed no abnormalities. Treatment : The patient underwent a course of RT. EAF readings were 70-80 on most points. The RV emitter was selected based on EAF. Treatment was conducted daily for 7 days, followed by treatment a week later. Results : Daily improvement. The frequency of blinking decreased to normal. Remission was maintained for a year. No side effects were observed.

Patient U., 62 years old, a woman, was treated for 2 years in a therapeutic clinic in Johor Hospital. She once had an acute episode of air shortage, accompanied by rapid heartbeat and orthopnea. She was hospitalized for two weeks and diagnosed with thyrotoxic cardiomyopathy. Left ventricular heart failure was observed. She was discharged on the 8th day. Orthopnea decreased after a few days in the hospital, but other symptoms like chest pain, fainting, increased sleepiness, and rapid heartbeat persisted for 3 weeks. The patient could not stand or walk. Due to extreme weakness, she constantly wanted to lie down, could not sit for more than 5 minutes, and could not feed herself. She also suffered from constipation and insomnia. Symptoms persisted until she sought treatment at Infra Life Clinic. ECG : Atrial fibrillation. Echo : Left atrial dilation, mitral valve thickening, moderate myocardial dystrophy of the left ventricle, and 52% filling. Treatment started with the following prescription : T. Carbimazole 15 mg tds, T. Propanolol 40 mg bd, T. Furosemide 40 mg bd, T. Slow K, 2 bd, T. Digoxin 0.125 mg OD. The patient took these medications, but since discharge, she was bedridden due to severe weakness. Based on her physical condition, Infra Life Clinic was hesitant to start IR therapy, as the outcome could be unpredictable, and doctors did not want to take responsibility for any worsening. However, her family insisted on a trial course of resonant IR therapy as they felt helpless watching her condition. EAF readings : Low on most points, below 10, many points at 0-12. On the meridians of the lymphatic system, lungs, large intestine, nervous system, circulation, allergy, organ degeneration, heart, and small intestine around 0-20. At least one point on each of the aforementioned meridians registered '0'. On many points, readings were 0, 4, 6 or <10. On the following meridians, readings were 12-30: pancreas, spleen, liver, joints, stomach, gallbladder, kidneys, and bladder. After using the ZB emitter, readings on most points increased to 40, BP 95/65. When selecting emitters by EAF, the patient did not respond to any emitters except the general ZB, where readings increased from 10 to 40 on the meridians of organ degeneration and circulation. After 2 minutes, the readings started to decrease slowly, and the treatment was stopped at a reading of 25. The next day, before starting treatment, most readings were higher at 10-20, and she could tolerate a session up to 5 minutes. A few hours after the first session, at home, she could sit longer, slept well, and had an easy bowel movement. After the second session, she could stand and walk a short distance. By the third session, readings were 20-30 compared to 10-20. After 5 sessions, she could stand for half a prayer, and after 7 sessions, she could walk and stand for the whole prayer. After 10 sessions, the patient felt significantly better and could do light housework. She almost fully returned to her original physical state. Treatment continued weekly, with 2 sessions before it was stopped. Further improvement was noted; she feels well, except for occasional rapid heartbeat. Her last visit for a follow-up was 10 months later. Since then, she has been in good health.

A 23-year-old patient was admitted with a diagnosis of toxoplasmosis. Complaints upon admission included headache, general weakness, lumbar and inguinal pain, frequent blood pressure increases up to 130/90 - 140/80 mmHg, joint pains, and nausea. On examination, joints appeared unchanged but painful upon palpation, Wright-Huddleson test positive (1:100), RFIA for toxoplasmosis 1:80. Treatment : RC(b) on a floating scheme, RC(s) on "interest" zones, GI(b) from 10 to 40 minutes according to the scheme, GI(s) on the stomach, intestines, kidneys, liver, and pancreas for 10 minutes each, KL(b) for 10 minutes, ZB(b) for 10 minutes twice a week. Results : Headache, weakness, and nausea disappeared on the 3rd-4th day of treatment. Joints were pain-free by the 6th day, Wright-Huddleson test, and RFIA for toxoplasmosis negative after 2 weeks.

A patient presented with complaints of thyroid gland enlargement. EAF readings at the thyroid points were above normal. When emitters were applied to the thyroid area, normalization of readings was not observed. When the GI(s) emitter was directed at the lung area (where EAF readings were below normal), normalization was noted not only on the lung points but also on the thyroid points.

A 50-year-old patient presented with complaints of thyroid gland enlargement. EAF readings on thyroid and lung points were below normal. Only lung points tested positive for infection and disease nosodes. Testing determined that normalization of thyroid readings was achieved by applying an emitter to the lung area. This is explained by the fact that a disease in the lungs led to thyroid functional disturbances. Due to compensatory functions necessary for normal body functioning, the thyroid became overloaded, which was reflected in the below-normal EAF readings.

A 42-year-old patient presented with complaints of thyroid gland enlargement, weakness, sleepiness, and dry skin. EAF readings below normal were determined on points of the thyroid, intestines, and lungs. On all other points, they were within normal limits. No emitters were found to normalize thyroid function when directly applied. When the GI emitter was applied to the lung area, normalization of readings was observed at both lung and thyroid points. This fact indicates a reduction in the compensatory function of the thyroid due to the pathological process in the lungs.

A patient born in 1958. Clinical diagnosis - Nodular toxic goiter. Accompanying - severe anemia grade III. Complaints include neck pain (in the thyroid projection), a sensation of a foreign body, shortness of breath, loss of consciousness, pale skin, hot flashes at bedtime, and a subcutaneous hardening on the left foot the size of a nut. Symptoms began half a year ago. The patient was examined at the Institute of Endocrinology. During the examination, severe anemia was detected. Before coming to us, she received treatment at the blood transfusion institute. After the treatment, her condition slightly improved, but complaints of neck pain persisted. An endocrinologist recommended surgery. Past illnesses : ARVI, catarrhal angina, periodontitis, anemia. No harmful habits. No family history of the disease. On examination : General condition relatively satisfactory. Skin and visible mucous membranes clean, pale. Throat calm. Peripheral lymph nodes not enlarged. Musculoskeletal system - there is spinal deformity (scoliosis). Visually: thyroid diffusely enlarged, grade III. Consistency is firm-elastic. In the lungs - vesicular breathing. Heart sounds clear, slight systematic murmur at the apex. BP - 90/60. Abdomen soft, non-painful. Liver and spleen not palpable. Bowel movements normal. Laboratory data : Thyroid function test - thyroid image deformed due to the absence of the upper pole and middle zone of the right lobe. Left lobe and isthmus enlarged. Central thyroid function within normal limits. Conclusion: extensive "cold" defect of accumulation, replacing the volume of the upper pole and middle zone of the right lobe. Compensatory hypertrophy of the left lobe and isthmus. Ultrasound : from January 12, 1998, thyroid gland - right lobe 39x25 mm, where two nodules are visible - 16x11 mm, and 17x15 mm. Left lobe - 35x25 mm, one nodule - 17x11 mm. In both lobes, smaller nodules of 5 and 7 mm are visible. Conclusion: Nodular goiter. In line with our assumptions about the causes and mechanisms of this disease's development, treatment focused on the lung area and increasing the functional activity of the adrenal glands, gallbladder (as a source of free cholesterol when exposed to appropriate emitters), and intestines, which are primarily responsible for delivering necessary energy and building materials. A patient born in 1988 was admitted to the dermatology department of TashPMI clinic from Angren city, complaining of a thickening on the skin of the left frontal bone, left supraorbital area, extending to the bridge of the nose and hairy scalp, resembling a saber cut, loss of appetite, weakness, and rapid fatigue. According to his mother, he has been ill for 2.5 years. The illness was preceded by follicular tonsillitis, after which a painless, dense, shiny erythematous linear area appeared on the skin of the left frontal bone. Subsequently, the lesion slowly enlarged, extending to the hairy scalp with large focal alopecia, to the left supraorbital ridge and the bridge of the nose. The distal edge of the lesion hardened, while the proximal (on the hairy scalp) was replaced by brown pigmentation, with the skin within the lesion gradually atrophying. The patient had repeatedly visited a local dermatologist; localized scleroderma of linear form was diagnosed, several courses of antibiotic therapy, resorptive, vitamin, and hormone therapy were carried out. There was virtually no effect; the dermatological process progressed. Dermatological examination : Asymmetric, non-inflammatory, located on the skin of the left frontal bone, left supraorbital ridge, extending in a saber cut pattern to the bridge of the nose. The process involves the hairy scalp, where there is large focal alopecia. The pathological focus is clearly demarcated from the surrounding tissue, slightly recedes, has a purplish-red border. Within the lesion, the skin is atrophied, parchment-like, fused with surrounding tissues, does not fold. No subjective sensations. There is marked facial asymmetry with signs of hemiatrophy and anophthalmia. Downy hairs on the left forehead are completely gone, the left eyebrow is significantly thinner than the right (see picture). Skin temperature on the left bone is 0.8-1.2°C lower than on the right. A pediatrician found no internal organ pathology. No visible pathology on the overview radiograph. An ENT doctor diagnosed chronic compensated tonsillitis. In the dermatology department of TashPMI clinic, the patient received 15 sessions of RT. Both general and local emitters were used: GI - general action with gradually increasing exposure time from 15 to 65 minutes, KL - on the hypothalamus area for 15 minutes; ZB - directly on the affected area - 15-20 minutes. Simultaneously, the patient received medication therapy: lidase, vitamin B1, B6, nicotinic acid, ascorbic acid. No local ointment therapy was applied. After treatment, general condition improved, sleep and appetite normalized. In the pathological focus, the peripheral purplish rim disappeared, the scleroderma plaque became softer, its edges slightly smoothed, the skin began to fold slightly, pigmentation decreased. Pre-capillary collaterals develop around the atrophy focus. The patient was recommended a repeat treatment course after a three-week break.

A 45-year-old married man with chronic renal failure due to obstructive uropathy from kidney stones. Six years ago, he had kidney stones, which led to cystolithotripsy (stone fragmentation) and subsequent surgical lithotomy (stone removal). Since then, urine volume has decreased, and hypertension developed. He takes atenolol and nifedipine at 10 mg. Further observation revealed progressive renal failure and kidneys significantly reduced in size. Hemodialysis was started 6 months ago, 3 times a week. The patient sought treatment at our clinic but came very irregularly due to time spent on hemodialysis. For the first 2 weeks, treatment was conducted 3 times a week, then 2 times over 3 weeks. He was advised to collect urine in a container, measure the volume with a syringe, and keep records. Urine output remained unchanged over the past 6 months. Results : From the start of treatment, urine output increased as follows: Before treatment — 80 ml/day 5th day — 115 ml/day 7th day — 125 ml/day 14th day — 145 ml/day After 14 sessions, urine volume did not change and remained at 130-145 ml/day. Side Effects : On the day of treatment, the patient sometimes felt a mild headache that did not interfere with work. Comments : Urine volume increased by 60-70%, but the baseline is still very low to consider discontinuing hemodialysis. Treatment is quite limited for hemodialysis patients if the baseline is low. With continued treatment, further urine increase might be possible, but to what extent is unknown. However, one might expect a doubling of urine volume before reaching a plateau. In this case, the urine volume increased, but the patient could not come on schedule, only once a week, as he spends 3-4 hours on dialysis 3 times a week at the dialysis center.

A 55-year-old male patient. Chronic renal failure due to chemotherapy for stomach cancer. Surgery for stomach cancer was performed, achieving remission. The patient is currently on hemodialysis twice a week. Resonant therapy was applied to improve kidney function. Before the course, urine volume was approximately 500 ml/day. After a two-week course, urine output significantly increased to 700 ml/24 hours. Hemodialysis is still required twice a week. No side effects were observed. Comments : Therapy can increase urine volume in chronic renal failure, but it's better not with such a low baseline as in this case.

A 41-year-old female patient. Chronic renal failure developed due to kidney stone disease. She was operated on, but chronic renal failure had already set in. The patient is on continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (4 bags per day) for 2 years. Edema appears and disappears, skin pallor. Hypertension, taking nifedipine 10 mg tablets and prazosin 1 mg tablets. Both kidneys are very small (shrunken). Before treatment, daily urine volume was around 20-25 ml. The patient underwent a 30-day therapy course. Results : Urine volume increased daily or over several days as follows: 40 ml - 50 ml - 60 ml - 70-80 ml - 110 ml - 120 ml - 125 ml over the monthly period. The increase in flat urine level after 20 days of treatment is still insufficient to allow the patient to stop dialysis, but the overall condition has noticeably improved. Previously, she was unable to do housework due to fatigue and lack of energy. Since starting treatment, she can manage household chores all day and feels an increase in productivity. Treatment resulted in a significant 600% increase in urine compared to the initial level, but further treatment is not expected to increase urine volume further. During the therapy course, the patient experienced painless hematuria for 3 days. She was referred to a surgeon, underwent an ultrasound, which revealed a small stone in the right ureter that disappeared with continued treatment. No complications were noted. Comments : Even with a significant increase in urine output, the patient remains on dialysis at the same level (3-4 bags per day). Therefore, this method is not recommended for patients with chronic renal failure if their pre-treatment urine volume was very low. This method cannot help patients discontinue dialysis but might be beneficial for those with a urine volume over 500 ml/day.

Patient S., born in 1977, came to our clinic with a diagnosis of cytomegalovirus infection complicated by habitual late miscarriage. Over the last 2 years, she experienced two spontaneous miscarriages at 6-7 months of pregnancy, with fetuses showing signs of hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, and anasarca. Upon admission, she complained of aching lower abdominal pain, back pain, and copious purulent-bloody vaginal discharge. The cytomegalovirus test was positive (1:20). Discharge analysis: yeast, numerous cocci. Ultrasound showed chronic endometritis, chronic adnexitis, ovarian cysts. After ten days of therapy with antiviral, anti-inflammatory, and immunostimulatory emitters, combined with the "CT" setup, clinical manifestations of the disease disappeared. A repeat cytomegalovirus test two weeks after starting therapy was negative, and no echopathology was found on the ultrasound of the uterus and ovaries. Another patient, born in 1976, presented with complaints of constant aching lower abdominal pain, painful menstruation, subfebrile body temperature, copious purulent vaginal discharge, and frequent urination with unpleasant sensations. From the history : Ill for 2 years, repeatedly received medical treatment without effect. On Examination: Diagnosed with chronic colpitis, urethritis, bilateral adnexitis. Laboratory data: Blood test for cytomegalovirus positive; discharge analysis: marked leukocytosis, chlamydia, staphylococci, and yeast fungi detected. The treatment course consisted of 24 sessions. Antiviral, antibacterial, and anti-inflammatory emitters were used. Immune correction and normalization of the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems were also conducted. Results: On the 7th day, normalization of body temperature was noted, pain disappeared by the 10th day, and significant reduction in vaginal discharge by the 15th day. On repeat examination, cytomegalovirus was not found in the blood. In the discharge analysis, leukocytes were within normal limits, chlamydia was not detected, and staphylococci and yeast fungi were present in minimal amounts.

The patient complains of frequent headaches. EAF readings on vascular points are above normal, while on large intestine points, they are lower. Simultaneously, normalization of readings on the vascular points was noted. A 30-year-old female patient. Complaints : For 2 months, the patient had chronic dry cough, weight loss, and loss of appetite. Chest X-ray showed a fluffy shadowing in the right upper lobe. However, sputum for AFB was negative. The clinical diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis was made, and a standard regimen of medication including rifampicin was prescribed. The patient came to us on the second day, hoping that resonant therapy with an antibacterial emitter might help alongside medications. Treatment started using GI and RC emitters. Due to high EAF readings on the liver, the RC emitter was also applied to the liver. Treatment was conducted every other day as the patient felt very tired after each session. An interesting phenomenon was observed: on treatment days, urine was clear and colorless, on days without treatment, urine was reddish. This phenomenon was observed over 7 days, where on 3 treatment days, the urine was clear, and on 4 non-treatment days, it was reddish, although the patient took the same dose of rifampicin. She was concerned that the IR radiation on the liver might reduce the effectiveness of the medication, as this method is not proven. We gave her the choice to continue treatment but without the liver emitter or to stop the course. She chose to proceed with only medication therapy. Side Effects : The primary symptom on IR therapy days was drowsiness. Comments : The observed phenomenon might be related to the significant influence on the liver's processing of medications in general or specifically rifampicin in this case or paracetamol in the previously described case.

The increase in flat urine level after 20 days of treatment is still insufficient to allow the patient to stop dialysis, but the overall condition has noticeably improved. Previously, she was unable to do housework due to fatigue and lack of energy. Since starting treatment, she can manage household chores all day and feels an increase in productivity. Treatment resulted in a significant 600% increase in urine compared to the initial level, but further treatment is not expected to increase urine volume further.

During the therapy course, the patient experienced painless hematuria for 3 days. She was referred to a surgeon, underwent an ultrasound, which revealed a small stone in the right ureter that disappeared with continued treatment. No complications were noted.

Comments

: Even with a significant increase in urine output, the patient remains on dialysis at the same level (3-4 bags per day). Therefore, this method is not recommended for patients with chronic renal failure if their pre-treatment urine volume was very low. This method cannot help patients discontinue dialysis but might be beneficial for those with a urine volume over 500 ml/day.

CYTOMEGALOVIRUS INFECTION

Patient S., born in 1977, came to our clinic with a diagnosis of cytomegalovirus infection complicated by habitual late miscarriage. Over the last 2 years, she experienced two spontaneous miscarriages at 6-7 months of pregnancy, with fetuses showing signs of hepatosplenomegaly, ascites, and anasarca. Upon admission, she complained of aching lower abdominal pain, back pain, and copious purulent-bloody vaginal discharge. The cytomegalovirus test was positive (1:20). Discharge analysis: yeast, numerous cocci. Ultrasound showed chronic endometritis, chronic adnexitis, ovarian cysts.

After ten days of therapy with antiviral, anti-inflammatory, and immunostimulatory emitters, combined with the "CT" setup, clinical manifestations of the disease disappeared. A repeat cytomegalovirus test two weeks after starting therapy was negative, and no echopathology was found on the ultrasound of the uterus and ovaries.

Another patient, born in 1976, presented with complaints of constant aching lower abdominal pain, painful menstruation, subfebrile body temperature, copious purulent vaginal discharge, and frequent urination with unpleasant sensations.

From the history

: Ill for 2 years, repeatedly received medical treatment without effect.

On Examination:

Diagnosed with chronic colpitis, urethritis, bilateral adnexitis. Laboratory data: Blood test for cytomegalovirus positive; discharge analysis: marked leukocytosis, chlamydia, staphylococci, and yeast fungi detected.

The treatment course consisted of 24 sessions. Antiviral, antibacterial, and anti-inflammatory emitters were used. Immune correction and normalization of the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems were also conducted.

Results:

On the 7th day, normalization of body temperature was noted, pain disappeared by the 10th day, and significant reduction in vaginal discharge by the 15th day. On repeat examination, cytomegalovirus was not found in the blood. In the discharge analysis, leukocytes were within normal limits, chlamydia was not detected, and staphylococci and yeast fungi were present in minimal amounts.

FREQUENT HEADACHES

The patient complains of frequent headaches. EAF readings on vascular points are above normal, while on large intestine points, they are lower. During emitter testing on the large intestine points, normalization of readings was observed after exposure with the GI emitter on the large intestine area, indicating an inflammatory process there. Simultaneously, normalization of readings on the vascular points was noted. After several sessions of IR therapy with the GI emitter on the intestine area, there was an increase in EAF readings on the large intestine points and normalization of the vascular points. Headaches significantly decreased.

EFFECT OF IR RADIATION ON A PATIENT TAKING RIFAMPICIN

A 30-year-old female patient.

Complaints

: For 2 months, the patient had chronic dry cough, weight loss, and loss of appetite.

Chest X-ray showed a fluffy shadowing in the right upper lobe. However, sputum for AFB was negative. The clinical diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis was made, and a standard regimen of medication including rifampicin was prescribed.

The patient came to us on the second day, hoping that resonant therapy with an antibacterial emitter might help alongside medications.

Treatment started using GI and RC emitters. Due to high EAF readings on the liver, the RC emitter was also applied to the liver. Treatment was conducted every other day as the patient felt very tired after each session.

An interesting phenomenon was observed: on treatment days, urine was clear and colorless, on days without treatment, urine was reddish. This phenomenon was observed over 7 days, where on 3 treatment days, the urine was clear, and on 4 non-treatment days, it was reddish, although the patient took the same dose of rifampicin. She was concerned that the IR radiation on the liver might reduce the effectiveness of the medication, as this method is not proven. We gave her the choice to continue treatment but without the liver emitter or to stop the course. She chose to proceed with only medication therapy.

Side Effects

: The primary symptom on IR therapy days was drowsiness.

Comments

: The observed phenomenon might be related to the significant influence on the liver's processing of medications in general or specifically rifampicin in this case or paracetamol in the previously described case.
